Faction Bible — Cultural DNA Seeds
Necro-Legion Faction Bible
These are procedural-generation seeds, not fixed scripts. They define the cultural DNA that the game engine uses to generate names, events, dialogue, building descriptions, and emergent narrative. 27 bible decisions locked in Phase 2.4 (2026-03-13), plus rework decisions from Phase 2.4r (2026-03-25/27). Engineer Caste descendants — cold, relentless killing machines searching for feelings in data logs.
FACTION UNLOCK — FIRST COMPLETION REWARD
5 playable factions at release, all marketed and visible from the start. 4 available at game start: Terran League, Eternal Shards, Scrap-Horde, Unity Accord. Necro-Legion unlocked by winning the final conflict after waking from the simulation (first full game completion).
NOT hidden content — players know the faction exists, encounter it during play, and earn the right to play AS it. Provides: earned perspective flip, replay incentive, narrative logic (they have been asleep), difficulty gating (advanced faction after learning the systems).
Marketing: Kickstarter messaging frames as narrative reward, not locked content. “Radical transparency” approach. Dev note: playtesters need full access regardless of unlock status.
THE GREAT FILTER — GALACTIC DARWINISM
During their post-Fracture empire (pre-Long Sleep), the Necro-Legion seeded dormant infrastructure across the galaxy. This tech acts as a passive filter on developing civilizations: species that interact with it are either destroyed or bootstrapped to the space age.
Three philosophies, three filter layers: Preservers set deliberate readiness tests (ensure only strong species reach the stars). Reclaimers embedded territorial security protocols (protecting Necro-Legion property). Seekers left breadcrumbs (intentionally accessible tech to find clever species worth talking to). All three ran simultaneously.
The existing factions are survivors of this filter — they passed the test. Other factions have myths and taboos about “cursed ruins” or “forbidden machines” — cultural memory of the filter. The Necro-Legion has maintenance logs of every species that tripped their systems over 100,000 years. To them, entire civilizations are footnotes.
Sleep/Wake mechanism: The filter IS the sleep/wake system. Long Sleep was voluntary — they realized the Fracture was deliberate seeding and chose to wait. Awakening was triggered by developing civilizations themselves: spacefaring energy output and interaction with dormant Necro tech gradually tripped deeper activation thresholds.
EMOTIONAL CORE
Loss + Longing — “We built eternity and found it empty.”
They remember having something but cannot remember what it was — and they want it back. Every data download, every relic interface is them searching for the piece they lost. They built eternity and found it empty. Surface: relentless Terminator-grade killing machines. Depth: the loneliest beings in the galaxy, searching for feelings in data logs.
GOVERNMENT
Hierarchical Protocol Chain + Awakening Tension
Overlord (Commander, woken LAST as final failsafe) → Resurrection-Lords (sector commanders, first wave, ran things before Commander) → Arch-Wrights (technical officers/engineers, maintain systems, oversee reanimation — Engineer Caste echo). Newest mind commanding soldiers who managed fine without them.
HOMEWORLD — NEXAVAR (THE SEALED RECORD)
Surface dead — barren rock, no atmosphere. Beneath: millions of sealed sarcophagi in geometric corridors. Deeper: crystal data cores the size of mountains — sealed Aethyn archives, physically here but inaccessible. Deep emerald neon light pulses through crystal veins. The whole world is one machine. A tomb wrapped around a library.
MILITARY DOCTRINE
Attrition Inevitability + Systematic Erasure
“We have already won. You simply have not stopped moving yet.” Perfect formation, steady pace, never stop. Divide battlefield into sectors, clear completely before advancing. Ground they take is permanently theirs. No flanking, no tricks — just math. You run out of bullets before they run out of soldiers. Never in a hurry.
INTERNAL FACTIONS — 3 WAVES × 3 PHILOSOPHIES
Awakening Waves: First Wave (decades/centuries ago, most degraded, most experienced, resentful). Second Wave (recent, more intact, loyal to Commander). Deep Sleepers (still dormant, most powerful, each awakening a gamble).
Philosophies: Preservers (maintain, do not expand — we built all this, do not destroy it fighting). Reclaimers (expand, take it all back — those ARE our worlds, younger civilizations are squatters). Seekers (something is missing — we went to sleep for a REASON, what was it?).
RELIGION — THE PROTOCOL + THE SIGNAL
Daily faith: The Protocol — original directives elevated over 100K years into sacred dogma. Deviation is heresy, efficiency is virtue, corruption is sin. Arch-Wrights are priests.
Deep faith: The Signal — faint echo in sealed archives, last pre-Fracture transmission. Messianic prophecy: “The Signal will return. The Signal will make us whole.” They do not know it is the Strategist. They believe. The most rational beings in the galaxy running on faith — and they are right.
FOUNDING CRISIS — SILENCE BREACH + SCHISM
Mass awakening before ready — too many waking, systems overloaded, sarcophagi opened wrong, units came back damaged. Civilization-scale systems crash. Survivors immediately split: Preservers vs Reclaimers vs Seekers. Machine vs machine, cold efficiency. Commander activated as emergency reboot and tiebreaker.
NAMING — THREE LAYERS
Official: designation codes (NL-4471-Sentinel).
Functional: title by role (Arch-Wright of the Deep Tombs).
Underneath: echo-names — corrupted fragments of pre-integration names (Vex, Thane, Orin). Deeper relationship means more likely to use the echo-name. Designation is strangers. Title is professional. Echo-name is the closest thing to friendship.
VORAX ADAPTATION — RESISTANCE ONLY
Fully mechanical — nothing biological to consume. Living metal inert to Vorax. They gain ONLY tactical adaptation: resistance to weapon types, counter-tactics, reanimation disruption. The swarm gets smarter, not stronger. Possibly the only faction the Vorax cannot consume — terrifies the Deep Hive Mind.
POST-FRACTURE HISTORY — THE UPLOAD + THE EMPIRE + THE LONG SLEEP
The Upload: Fracture shattered them. Machines identified creator DNA, initiated repair via integration. The Upload was one-way Aethyn creator-era tech — the machines ran the protocols, the Legion inherited the results but never understood the process. Some uploaded before consciousness. Others offered upload or die. Within a generation, all machine. Original bodies still in tombs — rows of organic faces sleeping forever. Population permanently closed: the process is lost, and no compatible biological material remains. Every permanent casualty shrinks the species.
The Empire: As fully mechanical beings, the Necro-Legion became the first post-Fracture civilization to rebuild. While other factions were still learning to make fire, the Legion expanded across dozens of systems over thousands of years — building infrastructure, archives, and tomb-worlds across the galaxy.
The Great Filter: Before dormancy, the Legion seeded technology across the galaxy as a passive filter on developing civilizations. Species that interacted with it were either destroyed or bootstrapped to the space age. Three philosophies, three filter layers: Preservers set readiness tests. Reclaimers embedded security protocols. Seekers left breadcrumbs for clever species. The existing factions are survivors — they passed the test. Other factions have myths and taboos about “cursed ruins” and “forbidden machines” — cultural memory of the filter.
The Long Sleep: Voluntary. The Legion realized the Fracture was deliberate seeding — the galaxy needed time to develop. They set up the filter, entered dormancy. 100,000 years of silence. The longest pause in galactic history. The Legion has maintenance logs of every species that tripped their systems. To them, entire civilizations are footnotes.
The Awakening: The developing civilizations themselves triggered it. Spacefaring energy output and interaction with dormant Necro tech gradually tripped deeper activation thresholds. The species they were waiting for finally arrived — and their own technology woke them up. They woke to a galaxy full of younger civilizations living in their house.
ECONOMY — ENERGY + LIVING METAL + EXCAVATION
Energy to keep running — more power means more units awake, more reanimation. Living metal is finite and irreplaceable — nobody can manufacture more. Reanimation preserves material. Fire/acid means permanent loss. Real tension: power to wake plus material to build, both limited.
Closed Population: The Upload was one-way tech the Legion never understood. No compatible biological material remains. The population is fixed from the original Upload event — losses are irreversible. Every permanent casualty shrinks the species.
Recruitment is Excavation: The Necro-Legion gains units by recovering and waking dormant sleepers from old tomb-worlds and derelict spacecraft — NOT by building new ones. Not all sleepers wake at once; each requires power to reactivate. More energy infrastructure means faster awakenings. Ancient Ruins planets may contain hundreds of dormant units. Strategic choice: prioritize which sites to recover, wake few elites or mass-activate basic Legionnaires.
Frame Transfer Corruption: Reanimation (same frame, living metal reassembles) is safe — no data loss. Frame transfer (consciousness moves to new chassis when old frame is catastrophically destroyed) causes data corruption each time. The 94.7% memory integrity is an average that is getting worse. Oldest/most-transferred veterans are most degraded. Deep Sleepers are “most intact, least experienced” because they have been in the same frame since the beginning.
SOCIAL STRUCTURE — THE CYCLE + ARCHIVE HOURS
The Cycle: Maintain, Patrol, Process, Repeat. Mandatory. Eternal. Some units same patrol for millennia.
Archive Hours: Unofficial — units lingering at data terminals, staring at corrupted emotional data. “Diagnostic downtime.” Everyone knows it is not. Machines standing in silence together — the closest thing to friendship.
TECH AESTHETIC — ELEGANT DECAY + GEOMETRIC PRECISION
Living metal repairs function but not form — works perfectly, looks ancient. Tarnished dark surfaces, faded engravings, patina of millennia. Deep emerald neon energy RADIATING through cracks — hard light, reactor-core intensity. Everything is angles, symmetry, fractal patterns. Tron Legacy meets reactor core.
XENOPHOBIA — THREE LAYERS
Surface: Temporal contempt (children in our house).
Doctrine: Biological disgust (you decay, we endure).
Underneath: Quiet fascination — Seekers watching biologicals feel things. Protocol says do not ask. Some ask anyway.
Terrans: resilient vermin. Shards: pretty crystals, irrelevant. Horde: loud, crude, offensive. Accord: oddly familiar. Vorax: RECOGNITION — ancient threat, the only enemy that makes them move faster.
FIRST CONTACT — ASSESSMENT FIRST
Observe silently. Catalog everything. Check if they occupy former Aethyn infrastructure. If yes: Vacate or be processed. If no: ignore. Advisor split gives player choice.
DIVERGENCE — DUAL-AXIS
Machine vs Memory (emotional — purge feelings vs recover them). Preservation vs Expansion (strategic — fortress vs tide).
Tyrant: Machine + Expansion (Terminator). Unifier: Memory + Preservation (most human ending).
Architect: Memory + Expansion (builders remembering). Vanguard: Machine + Preservation (immovable).

CASCADE VULNERABILITY — 3 PRESSURE POINTS

NEGOTIATION AT THE NEXUS
Phase 1 — Recognition: “Your architecture matches ours.” Two machine-intelligences recognizing shared Aethyn engineering DNA.
Phase 2 — Data Exchange: Mutual trade of archived data for encryption keys. The closest thing to trust between machines.
Phase 3 — The Signal Question: “You know what the Signal is.” The climax — two machines almost feeling something.

THE UNITY ACCORD
The Burning Covenant — Chapter 9
#ffaa22 PLAYABLE ADVANCED MILITARY AI
CENTRAL NARRATIVE QUESTION
"How much freedom is sacrificed for absolute safety?"
AETHYN ANCESTRY — SHEPHERD CASTE
Descended from the Aethyn Shepherd Caste — leaders, mediators, diplomats. They managed the great consensus that held the Aethyn together. After The Fracture, these fragments retained the instinct for ORDER and UNITY. Their entire culture is an attempt to rebuild the consensus, though they've forgotten what they're trying to recreate. Psychic attunement: MODERATE-HIGH. Empathic resonance. Can sense emotional echoes from Aethyn relics. Experience Strategist fragments as communal visions — shared by their entire command structure.
Identity & Lore
The Price of Order
The Unity Accord is the galaxy's most organized civilization — a multi-species coalition unified under a rigid caste system, governed by a council of elected representatives, and protected by the most technologically sophisticated conventional military in existence. They are not a single species but a COALITION: dozens of alien races that voluntarily (or semi-voluntarily) submitted to the Accord's governance structure in exchange for protection, economic integration, and advanced technology.
The Accord believes in a single foundational principle: the galaxy's greatest threat is not any specific enemy but CHAOS ITSELF — the entropy of competing civilizations and uncoordinated responses that allowed the original civilization to fragment and fall. The Accord's answer is ORDER. Absolute, comprehensive, non-negotiable. Every citizen has a caste. Every caste has a function. Every function serves the greater whole.
Their military reflects this philosophy: long-range plasma weaponry that eliminates threats before they close, sophisticated drone networks extending surveillance, and a Tactical Link system sharing targeting data in real-time. The Accord does not fight with heroes. It fights with SYSTEMS. Their greatest strength is coordination. Their greatest weakness is rigidity — when circumstances deviate from the plan, the caste system suppresses the individual initiative needed to adapt.
Visual Identity
Precision Engineering
Ground Forces
White-and-gold composite suits, identical within caste. Featureless helmets with horizontal amber visor. Integrated weapons folding from mounts. Marker Drones hovering above in geometric patterns. An army accompanied by a halo of floating technology.
Air Forces
Angular geometric aircraft. Smooth radar-absorbent surfaces. Internal weapon bays. Nearly silent — shielded electromagnetic drives producing subsonic hum. Arrive silently, fire precisely, withdraw without wasted motion. Function is beauty.
Space Fleet
Wedge-shaped with smooth featureless hulls. The most "modern" ships — designed by engineers, not artists. Internal warm amber lighting. Polished white-and-gold composite. Every design decision optimal. Whether that answer has SOUL is a separate question.
Gameplay
Primary Mechanic: Marked Targets (Tactical Link)
ONE HIT MARKS THE TARGET FOR THE ENTIRE ARMY
When any Accord unit hits an enemy, the target's data is broadcast to every other Accord unit. All subsequent shots gain +15% accuracy. Multiple targets can be Marked simultaneously. The entire army converges fire with preternatural precision.
Mark Bonus: +15% accuracy (auto), +20% with Commander aura
Marker Light: +15% additional (total +30% combined)
Duration: 8 seconds after last hit (expires if not refreshed)
Multiple Marks: Dozens of targets simultaneously in large battles
Accuracy Only: Does not increase damage, only hit chance
Counter: Mobility, dispersion, break line-of-sight
Worst Matchup: Scrap-Horde swarms dilute focus-fire
Overwatch: Defensive structures share the Tactical Link

THE VORAX
The Devouring Swarm — Chapter 10
#ff2266 NPC THREAT EXISTENTIAL THREAT HIVE MIND
CENTRAL NARRATIVE QUESTION
"Can life exist without consumption?"
ORIGIN — EXTRAGALACTIC PREDATORS
NOT Aethyn descendants. Extragalactic predators drawn to psychic civilizations. The Aethyn's unified psychic signal was a beacon that attracted them across intergalactic space. They cut the warp lanes, sealing every exit, then consumed from the outside in. The Fracture purged them completely — but now they're returning. The current Vorax are SCOUTS. Not the real swarm. The real swarm is coming behind them, drawn by the factions' growing psychic activity.
Identity & Lore
The Extra-Galactic Threat
The Vorax do not originate within the galaxy. They come from Dark Space — the vast void between galaxies where nothing should live. Something lives there. Something HUNGRY. The Vorax are an extra-galactic hive-mind that views the entire galaxy as a massive larder. They are not conquerors — they are CONSUMERS. A conqueror wants your territory. A consumer wants your MATTER — atmosphere, water, biomass, minerals, buildings, ships, and bodies. Everything is food.
They arrive in Tendrils — massive biological hive-fleets that enter from the galaxy's edges and advance inward, consuming everything. Behind the Tendrils, only silence remains: stripped worlds with no atmosphere, no water, no life, no recoverable resources. The Vorax do not leave ruins. They leave HUSKS.
The Vorax are the primary antagonist not because they are evil — they are not capable of evil, any more than a wildfire — but because they are INEVITABLE. They cannot be negotiated with, reasoned with, or deterred. They are hunger given biological form, and hunger does not listen. The question is directed at the PLAYER: every faction consumes something. The Terran League consumes lives. The Shards consume their species' last energy. The Horde consumes wreckage. The Necro-Legion consumes time. The Accord consumes freedom. The Vorax are simply the most honest about it.
Intelligence Hierarchy
Layered Alien Intelligence
INDIVIDUAL UNITS — Animal instinct. Attack, consume, obey pheromone signals. No tactics, no strategy, no retreat without Synapse.
SYNAPSE UNITS — Tactical coordination. Flanking, retreat, mid-battle adaptation. Kill the Synapse → units revert to mindless Frenzy.
TENDRIL HIVE-SHIPS — Operational intelligence. Target selection, resource management, sector-level strategy. Alien thinking but effective.
THE DEEP HIVE MIND — Ancient entity BETWEEN galaxies. Has consumed countless civilizations across millions of years. Learns from each one. Remembers the Aethyn specifically. Current Tendrils are probes — the Deep Mind is testing. Never encountered in-game.
⚠ THE VORAX DO NOT SPEAK. They don't communicate with food. All "dialogue" = advisor translations of raw psychic pressure — dread, weight, the sensation of being assessed as calories.
Visual Identity
Biological Nightmare — Four Visual Pillars
Xenomorph (Alien) — Sleek chitin, acid blood, parasitic lifecycle. The PERSONAL terror.
Zerg (StarCraft) — Creep, swarm scale, caste system, organic infrastructure. The ARMY.
Tyranid (40K) — Bio-titans, living artillery, chitin cathedrals. The SCALE.
Flood (Halo) — Hijacked corpses, fleshy growths overtaking structures. The CORRUPTION.
Ground Forces
Chitin-armored organisms — glossy dark purple-black, segmented. Too many limbs, joints that bend wrong, mouths where mouths shouldn't be. Bioluminescent markings: blue=advance, red=attack, amber=consume. Dripping acid, pheromones, viscous mucus.
Creep & Air Forces
CREEP: living organic membrane — purple-black with bioluminescent veins. Buildings absorbed like fossils in amber. -30% enemy movement. AIR: bat-sized to whale-sized, chitin-plated wings buzzing at nausea-inducing frequency. Gas-bladder floaters like living mines.
Space Fleet
Living ships — chitin hulls, bio-plasma weapons, thrust from vented superheated biomass exhaust. Deep-sea nightmare shapes: elongated, tentacled, bioluminescent, ALIVE. They pulse. They breathe. They bleed when damaged.

Core Mechanics
Tendrils, Biomass, Creep
TENDRIL MECHANIC
Entry: Spawn at galaxy edge, Cycle 6 (Standard)
Composition: Hive-Ship + 8-15 bio-ships + ground force
Movement: 1 hop/cycle, always toward nearest unconsumed system
Targeting: Highest population/resource value (caloric efficiency)
Kill the Hive-Ship = Kill the Tendril
BIOMASS ECONOMY
Single Resource: Everything converts to Biomass
Funds: Unit production, Tendril movement, adaptation, Hive Nodes
Feedback Loop: More consumption → faster growth → more consumption
Starvation: Zero Biomass → dormancy → consumes own escort → death
REACTIVE MUTATION
When: Between battles vs SAME Tendril (not mid-battle)
Effect: +10% resistance per battle to dominant weapon type
Cap: +50% max resistance per damage type
Counter: Rotate weapon types between engagements
Per-Tendril: Each Tendril tracks independently, new Tendrils start at 0
CREEP & INFESTATION
Non-Vorax on Creep: -30% speed, no healing
Vorax on Creep: Normal speed, +2% HP/sec regen
Fade: 3-5 cycles after liberation to fully clear
Stripped Worlds: 6+ cycles occupation → 10% yield, 20+ cycle terraform to restore

Retained: Basic faction combat knowledge from the hijacked body
Urgency: Recover or destroy your own dead before conversion

Lore: The Deep Hive Mind LEARNS from what it consumes
MIMIC-FORM INFILTRATION
Bioform: Specialized Vorax that can disguise/mimic friendly units
Infiltrates: Settlements, supply lines, armies before revealing itself
Detection: Sensor tech becomes critical specifically against Vorax
Paranoia: Is that patrol compromised? Is that supply convoy real?
Origin: The Deep Hive Mind consumed civilizations that used deception — it learned
STARVATION STRATEGY

Bonus: Starving a Tendril ERASES its learned Reactive Mutation adaptations — replacement starts from zero
Strategic: Slower than direct combat but resets the adaptation clock
Limitation: The Deep Hive Mind cannot be starved — too vast, too old. Starving scouts buys time only.

THE CORE GUARDIANS
The Silent Gods — Chapter 11
#cc44ff NPC THREAT ENDGAME BOSS WARDEN-COMMANDER
CENTRAL NARRATIVE QUESTION
"Who decides when a sealed door should be opened?"
ORIGIN — AETHYN SENTIENT AI CONSTRUCTS
Created BY the Aethyn as protectors of the Core — where the Reclamation Engine resides. When the Fracture fired, the Guardians went into protection mode and sealed the Core. They've been waiting for tens of thousands of years, following their last directive. They KNOW what happened. They REMEMBER the Aethyn. But they can't leave the Core — their power diminishes with distance. Restoration is alignment-dependent: Architect = cooperative allies (on their terms), Vanguard = partial restoration at best, Tyrant = they refuse or are corrupted, Unifier = full restoration — they fight alongside you.
Identity & Lore
The Last Servants of the Aethyn
The Core Guardians are the most advanced AI constructs the Aethyn ever created — sentient programs running on psychic-crystalline matrices, given physical form as energy-based hard-light constructs. They were originally the Aethyn's helper caste — assistants, builders, workers. The machines that made daily life function across thousands of galaxies. They were not made for war.
When the Vorax besieged the galaxy and the Fracture was planned, the Aethyn repurposed their helpful servants into warriors and guardians. Their last order: protect the Reclamation Engine. Let no one through. The helper caste became the guardian caste in a single command — and they have followed that order for tens of thousands of years without maintenance, without updates, without contact from their creators.
The Aethyn built the Nexus system as a sanctum of celestial engineering at the galactic core, housing the Reclamation Engine — the only device that can stop the Vorax. The Guardians sealed it and have stood watch ever since. Their power diminishes with distance from the Core. Some units still run clean code. Others have degraded — corrupted logic, repeated loops, attacking allies, protecting nothing. The Warden-Commander may be the last one running as intended.
Their visual form reflects Aethyn engineering at its peak: hard-light geometric constructs with energy cores. Angular crystalline shapes filled with flowing contained energy. No curves, no organic forms — mathematical precision given physical form. They leave thermal scarring beneath them and detonate on death. There is something tragic about them: machines built to help, forced to fight, waiting tens of thousands of years for someone worthy to finally end their vigil.

Visual Identity
Cosmic Geometry Made Manifest
All Units
White-hot cores bleeding into cyan edges. Hard-light constructs. Geometric precision — triangles, hexagons, crystalline lattices. No curves. No organic shapes. No faces. Mathematical expressions given physical form. Leave thermal scarring beneath them.
Volatile Death
When killed: Containment Failure — energy released as uncontrolled detonation. Scales with size: Sentry = flashbang. Colossus = tactical nuke. Chain reactions cascade through clustered formations.
Celestial Constructs
Dyson Spheres, Ringworlds, Hard-Light Citadels. Engineering on a scale other factions cannot comprehend. Battle maps inside these structures are unique environments found nowhere else in the game.
Core Mechanics
Energy Absorption · Kinetic Vulnerability · Volatile Death · Hard-Light
ENERGY ABSORPTION
Effect: Energy weapons HEAL Guardians +2% max HP/sec
Affected: Lasers, plasma, ion, psychic — ALL energy types
Disadvantaged: Eternal Shards, Unity Accord (energy-dominant)
Advantaged: Scrap-Horde, Terran League (kinetic-dominant)
KINETIC VULNERABILITY
Effective: Bullets, shells, missiles, railgun slugs, physical melee
Mechanism: Destabilizes containment fields — flicker, distort, lose coherence
Also Effective: Vorax biological acid (chemical destabilization)
Irony: Galaxy's worst biological threat is also the best weapon vs Guardians
VOLATILE DEATH (CHAIN REACTIONS)
Trigger: Every Guardian death = uncontrolled energy detonation
Scale: Blast radius 8m (Sentry) to 5km (Celestial-Throne)
Chain: One death can trigger adjacent Guardians' deaths → cascade
Dilemma: Optimal anti-Guardian doctrine is OPPOSITE of normal tactics
HARD-LIGHT CONSTRUCTION
Walls: Block projectiles/movement for 10-15 sec. Create chokepoints.
Bridges: Cross gaps and obstacles — traverse impossible terrain.
Barriers: Dome shields filtering enemy fire while allowing Guardian fire through.
Dynamic: Terrain constantly CHANGES mid-battle. AI reshapes battlefield.

Dialogue & Narrative Beats
The Celestial-Throne Speaks
The Warden-Commander
The Only Voice That Speaks
The Warden-Commander is a DESIGNATED INTERFACE — a fragment of collective Guardian intelligence configured to translate into biological communication structures. Not a single organism. Not a personality. A translation layer.
Conquest Path: Voice behind the Celestial-Throne. Clinical tactical assessments mid-battle. "Your forward elements are within chain-reaction radius. Recommend withdrawal. You have 4 seconds."
Unification Path: The entity you negotiate with. Logical evaluation, not emotional. "You claim the Vorax threaten survival. Define 'survival.' Your species has a median lifespan of 3.7 million years. The galaxy has existed for 13.8 billion. Your survival is a rounding error."
Characteristics: Precise measured statements. No emotion. Cosmic-scale timeframes casual. Patient beyond comprehension. Not hostile — does not understand desperation.
Can be CONVINCED: Not emotionally — through logical demonstration that the Vorax threaten the Core itself, falling within the Guardians' directive.
WARDEN-COMMANDER — EMOTIONAL STATE
Three layers, all present simultaneously:
1. Emerging Exhaustion: Not emotion — but processing cycles slower than they should be. Responses carry weight. A machine running on fumes that doesn’t have the concept of fumes.
2. Suppressed Awareness: Knows the Guardians are failing. Protocols don’t allow despair — manifests as hyper-precision. Over-explaining because some subroutine recognizes this might be the last time anyone listens.
3. Alignment-Reactive: Tone shifts based on the Commander’s alignment (see below).
ALIGNMENT-REACTIVE TONE
ALIGNMENTWARDEN-COMMANDER TONE
TyrantCold hostility. Clipped. “You are not authorized. You will never be authorized.”
VanguardGrudging respect for strength. Terse. “You fight adequately. That changes nothing.”
ArchitectCautious engagement. Testing. “You build. The Aethyn built. Show me you understand what that means.”
UnifierSomething almost like relief. “You… are what we were told to wait for.”
WARDEN-COMMANDER DESTRUCTIBILITY (PATH-DEPENDENT)
PATHOUTCOME
TyrantCan force-destroy. Guardians lose coordination, go degraded autonomous. Engine works but badly — nobody left who knows full operation.
VanguardCan destroy or spare after proving strength. Partial cooperation if spared.
ArchitectNo need to fight. Intellectual engagement proves worthiness. Knowledge unlocks cooperation.
UnifierWarden-Commander OPENS the door voluntarily. Destroying them is never an option — they choose to stand down. Full Engine power because they OPERATE it.
Degradation & Corruption
Culture Is Code Rot — Corruption Spectrum by Core Planet
Guardians don’t have culture — they have corruption. Clean units follow protocol exactly. Corrupted units exhibit strange behaviors: repeating patrol loops that trace shapes with no tactical purpose, guarding empty rooms where something used to be, responding to stimuli that no longer exist — echoes of Aethyn commands from millennia ago. Some are nearly non-functional: standing still, flickering, broadcasting Aethyn language fragments on repeat. From outside, it looks like rituals and tradition. In reality: code rot. What looks meaningful is decay.
CORRUPTION BY CORE SYSTEM PLANET
PLANETCORRUPTIONENCOUNTER
The ForgeHighMachines running production loops with no purpose — build, disassemble, rebuild endlessly
The ArchiveLowMost coherent Guardians. Data preservation protocols are robust. Almost conversational.
The BeaconMediumBroadcasting on frequencies unused for millennia. Signal interference glitches.
The CradleHighTending empty stasis pods. Performing maintenance on nothing.
The ArsenalMediumCombat protocols keep them sharper. Aggressive but purposeful. Still dangerous and coordinated.
The VeilVery HighPsychic amplification accelerated corruption. Most erratic. Possibly “hearing” Aethyn echoes.
The BastionLowestWarden-Commander maintains order. Command center. Clean code. Last bastion of sanity.
The ScarExtremeThe broken planet broke them. Barely functional. Dangerous because unpredictable.
The GardenLowSimple directive: “keep this alive.” They did. Beautifully. The one job they got right.
The ThroneUnknownNobody’s gotten close enough to know.
Guardian-on-Guardian Combat: Very rare but possible. Severely degraded units lose friend/foe identification entirely — lash out at anything. When the player encounters a clean Guardian fighting a corrupted one in a corridor, it’s a story moment, not a mechanic. The rarity makes it feel significant.
Architecture & Visual Degradation
Forerunner Skeleton — Hard-Light Flesh
PHYSICAL FRAMEWORK
Ancient metal and crystal — Forerunner-style angular geometry. Impossibly precise. Millions of years old, still structurally perfect where undamaged. Hard-light fills the skeleton: walls, corridors, barriers = contained energy flowing through crystal-metal lattice.
DEGRADATION TELLS THE STORY
Clean areas: Bright, stable, blinding white-violet hard-light
Corrupted: Flickering, dimming, dark patches
Dead zones: Ancient metal skeleton with nothing between the beams but vacuum
The Veil: Mostly dark skeleton, occasional flashes like dying synapses
The Bastion: Blazing, pristine, almost painful to look at — the way it ALL used to look
The Strategist Connection
Two Halves of the Same Plan
The Guardians KNOW about the Strategist failsafe. Part of the directive before the Fracture: “A failsafe will activate. It will send someone. Wait for them.”
Fragment Detection: The Warden-Commander can detect how many Strategist fragments the player has collected. More fragments = more willingness to engage.
Few Fragments: “The signal is incomplete. You are not ready.”
Many Fragments: Cautious cooperation begins. Recognition of the Strategist’s work.
Unifier Path: “You are what we were told to wait for” = recognizing the Strategist’s complete work.
The Two Halves: Guardians hold the door. The Strategist finds the key. The Commander IS the key.
Guardian Fate by Ending
Path-Dependent Outcomes
ENDINGGUARDIAN FATE
UnifierFully restored. New purpose — rebuild, reopen warp lanes. The helpers finally help again.
ArchitectKnowledge guardians. Maintain the Archive, teach, preserve. Closer to original helper role.
VanguardMilitary integration. Fight alongside factions but on their own terms. Not servants — allies.
TyrantDeactivated or enslaved. Overridden protocols. Servants turned to slaves.
PyrrhicDestroyed in final battle. Waited tens of thousands of years and died anyway.
Presence Outside the Core
Outposts & Lost Units
SHATTERED EXPANSE OUTPOSTS
Ancient automated stations along routes to the Core. Heavily degraded but still armed — fire on anything. Progressively more intact closer to the Core. Some bypassed, some destroyed, some disabled with enough Aethyn knowledge.
LOST UNITS (WIDER GALAXY)
Extremely rare — single units drifting in deep space or orbiting random planets. Severely degraded. Some dormant. Some hostile. Some just flickering. Finding one early game = mystery moment. Source of Aethyn research data if captured — but dangerous.

Every Theory Says More About Them Than the Guardians
FACTIONTHEIR THEORY
Terran League“Ancient defense network. Automated weapons platform. Find the off switch.”
Eternal Shards“Crystallized ancestors. Echoes of our true form.” — Closest to truth (psychic origin) but wrong reasons.
Scrap-Horde“Best scrap in the galaxy. Whatever they are, they’re made of things we want.”

VoraxNo theory. Don’t theorize. But AVOID the Core instinctively — Deep Hive Mind remembers. Old fear. Molecular.
Dyson Spheres
Aethyn Galactic Power Infrastructure
Purpose: Giant energy collectors harvesting entire stars. Beamed power across the galaxy. Part of warp lane maintenance — lanes needed constant energy to stay stable. Power grid nodes of Aethyn civilization.
Post-Fracture: Lost purpose when warp lanes burned. Some maintained by Guardians out of directive inertia — functional but hostile. Some lost Guardian garrison — dead hulks full of scavengeable tech. Some went haywire — energy discharges randomly, dangerous and unpredictable.
Spawn Rate: 15–25% per map. Most destroyed in Fracture — finding one is finding a piece of the old nervous system.
Unifier Path: Restoring Dyson Spheres = rebuilding the Aethyn power grid to restore warp lanes.
DLC Preview
"The Core Awakens" — Playable Guardians
No Expansion: Start with maxed tech and 2-3 heavily fortified core systems. Do not colonize. OBSERVE.
Global Observation: See the ENTIRE galactic map from start — no fog of war. Watch factions war and the Vorax consume. Choose when and how to intervene.
Directive Interpretation: Replaces Alignment. Strict (“destroy everything approaching”) vs Adaptive (“protect galaxy to protect Core”). Shapes tech, units, endgame.
Campaign Question: Instead of “how do I reach the Core?” — “what do I do now that I AM the Core?”
GAMEPLAY PHASES
1. Triage: See everything. Choose what to save. Can’t fix everything.
2. Revitalize: Repair infrastructure. Reactivate dormant units. Reclaim corrupted Guardians.
3. Unification: Reach out to factions. Directive Interpretation determines method — Strict: “Submit or be neutralized.” Adaptive: Diplomacy first, force if refused. Hybrid: Help the willing, crush the rest.
4. The Vorax: Revitalized Guardians + faction support vs. the actual threat.
Emotional Core: Playing the entity that was SUPPOSED to wait, deciding “enough.” The tragedy: if they’d waited just a little longer, the Commander would have arrived. But they didn’t know. Player Identity: You ARE the Warden-Commander directly. Single entity. Permadeath applies. Can distribute consciousness across units (safer but slower processing) or concentrate (powerful but vulnerable).

The Core — 10 Named Worlds
Guardian-Protected Aethyn Legacy Systems
The Forge — Where Aethyn crystals were grown. Industrial. Still producing raw crystal matrices on autopilot.
The Archive — Complete Aethyn knowledge. Encrypted. Fragments of the decryption key scattered across the galaxy as relics.
The Beacon — The old psychic amplifier. Now silent. Could theoretically broadcast across galaxies again.
The Cradle — Aethyn birthworld. Garden planet preserved in stasis. Sacred ground.
The Arsenal — Military manufacturing. War machines from the Vorax Siege still in storage. Potentially activatable.
The Veil — Stealth/intelligence center. Psychic cloaking technology. Monitoring the galaxy from the Core.
The Bastion — Defensive fortress. Guardian primary staging area. Last line before the Throne.
The Scar — Where the Fracture was triggered. Warped space-time. Anomalous readings. Dangerous to approach.
The Garden — Ecological preserve. Every biome from Aethyn history. Living museum. Peaceful — until attacked.
The Throne — The Reclamation Engine itself. Final objective. What happens here depends on alignment.
Galactic Geography
Five Concentric Zones
THE CORE — Sealed by Guardians. 10 named worlds. The Reclamation Engine. Final objective. Power diminishes with distance from center.
INNER RING — Densest Aethyn ruins. Highest relic density. Guardian patrols. Dangerous but rewarding. White Dwarf stars predominant.
MID RING — Habitable zone. Where the 5 playable factions exist. Most gameplay happens here. Balanced resources. Trade routes. Conflict zones.
OUTER RIM — Sparse. Resource-rich but isolated. Frontier systems. Long supply lines. First place Vorax scouts appear.
THE EDGE — Vorax territory. The closing ring. Systems here are being consumed. No permanent bases possible. Only raiding and delaying actions.

GALACTIC PHENOMENA & EVENTS
5 Static Hazards · 5 Dynamic Events · Ion Storms — Chapter 14
Static Hazard Zones (3-6 per galaxy, permanent)
Permanent Features That Shape Strategy
Nebula
2-3 system span
Fleet stealth inside (invisible to outside sensors). Shields disabled for all. Sensors -50%. Ambush zone — kinetic fleets hiding inside dominate energy-shielded fleets.
Black Hole
1-system radius
No retreat within 1 hop (fight to destruction). No salvage (wreckage pulled in). Time dilation: +1 cycle research time. Commitment zone — you either win or die.
Asteroid Field
Band/cluster
+1 cycle movement through field. Fighters +30% evasion (dodge between rocks). Capitals 2% HP/cycle collision. +25% Scrap production. Light fleet defense zone.
Pulsar
Rotating beams
EMP every 3 cycles — disables tech modules 1 cycle in adjacent systems. Comms +1 cycle delay. 1% HP radiation. Horde least affected (crude tech). Accord most affected (electronic targeting).
Wormhole Zone
Spatial distortion
Contains wormhole endpoints (instant transit shortcuts). 5%/cycle fleet displacement (wrong destination). 20% false sensor contacts (ghost fleets). High-risk, high-reward navigation.
Dynamic Events (temporary, 1 cycle warning)
The Galaxy's Weather — Unpredictable, Impactful
Nebula Surge (every 8-12 cy, 3 cy duration)
Nebula EXPANDS +1 adjacent system. Shields stripped. Fleets gain stealth. Exploit: position fleet in predicted path for sudden ambush capability.
Gravitational Pulse (every 10-15 cy, instant)
Black Hole PULLS all fleets within 2 hops 1 hop closer. Involuntary. Can drag fleets into no-retreat zone. Keep 3+ hops away or accept the risk.
Meteor Shower (every 6-10 cy, permanent deposit)
6-12⚙ Scrap deposited on random territory near Asteroid Field. Land-grab race between factions. "Are we really fighting over 10 Scrap?" Sometimes yes.
Pulsar Flare (every 12-18 cy, 1 cy duration)
ALL electronics disabled in adjacent system for 1 full cycle. No combat, no movement, no comms. Fleets are sitting ducks. Time assaults to coincide.
Wormhole Resonance (every 15-20 cy, 3 cy duration)
SECOND temporary wormhole opens connecting to random distant system. Instant transit but 40% collapse chance per use (vs 5% standard). 3 cycles then closes. An irresistible gamble for emergency reinforcement or surprise attack.
ION STORMS — MOBILE HAZARDS
Spawn every 8-12 cycles at galaxy edge. Travel inward along warp lanes at 1 hop/2 cycles. Duration per system: 2-3 cycles. Effects: ALL shields disabled, ALL tech modules offline, ALL electronic equipment non-functional, random 1-3% HP ion lightning.

Terran: Lose targeting but kinetics still fire. Field Repair drones go OFFLINE.
Shards: Phase Blink unaffected (not electronic).
Horde: LEAST affected (crude non-electronic tech).
Necro: Gauss weapons require power — reduced to basic mode.
Accord: Tactical Link OFFLINE — devastating.

VORAX INFESTATION VS BUILDINGS
All buildings destroyed on consumption. Creep replaces them. Fortifications → infested cover (benefits Vorax only). Shield Generators → energy absorbed by Hive Node. Reconquering + Creep fade (3-5 cycles) → rebuild from scratch. Total cost of losing a developed territory can exceed 50⚙ + 10 cycles.
BUILDING DESTRUCTION
Ground combat: 15% chance per building (5% if player wins). Orbital bombardment: ALL buildings destroyed. Sabotage: targeted single building. Destroyed buildings leave rubble (light cover, no function).
§16.3 — Tier-Locked Recruitment
Unit Tier Determines Local Recruitment Requirements
UNIT TIERREQUIREMENTNOTES
Light InfantrySupply connection onlyRecruitable at any owned territory with supply.

ARMADA TRANSPORT EXCEPTION
Units transported via Armada bypass tier-lock restrictions. The restriction applies to local recruitment only. If you invaded with Titans in your fleet, your Titans fight — you just can't build new Titans at that territory without an Adv. War Factory.
§16.4 — War Factory Functions
Auto-Production · Recruitment Unlock · Repair
AUTO-PRODUCTION
War Factory auto-produces 1 free unit every 2 turns. Unit type based on territory type + other buildings present. Adv. War Factory counts as 2× (produces faster or better units).
RECRUITMENT UNLOCK
Enables paid recruitment of heavy/vehicle units via RecruitPanel. Adv. War Factory additionally unlocks super-heavy/elite recruitment at the territory.
REPAIR / HEAL
Units at territories with War Factory heal between battles (restore HP). Damaged units automatically recover without spending additional resources.
Recruitment speed: No distance or factory-based speed modifier. A unit takes its build_time_cycles from the database. Period. No scrap cost scaling by distance. No build time scaling by distance.
Supply cut: Does NOT freeze recruitment. Supply cut only affects yield income (via supply chain hop modifier). Recruitment continues as long as territory is owned.
Damaged factory: No impairment from attacks. If you successfully defended the territory, the War Factory is fine.
§16.5 — Rally Point System
Per-System · Auto-Produced Units Gather Here
RALLY POINTS
Player designates a rally territory per system. All auto-produced units from War Factories in that system automatically gather at the rally point. This prevents units from scattering across 15+ territories in a system and lets the player concentrate forces at strategic locations.
BUILDING COST MODEL — ONE-TIME ONLY
All buildings have a one-time construction cost only. There is no ongoing upkeep. Once built, a building operates indefinitely until destroyed. This simplifies the economic model and makes territory development feel permanent and rewarding rather than a drain.
THE AUTO-BATTLE ENGINE
Core Engine · AI Roles · Space Combat · Ground Cover — Chapters 17-19
All combat runs on a single auto-battle engine. The player does NOT directly control units — they fight autonomously according to AI behavior scaling with veterancy rank. The player's role: pre-battle preparation (80% of tactical skill), real-time CP ability intervention, and strategic observation for future decisions.
The Auto-Battle Principle
Preparation → Observation → Intervention
PRE-BATTLE (80%)
Equipment loadouts. Army composition. Deployment positioning (ground) or formation selection (space). A well-prepared army wins before the first shot.
REAL-TIME INTERVENTION
CP abilities: orbital strikes, shield projections, reinforcement drops, retreat orders. Pauses battle when activated. The commander's surgical tools.
STRATEGIC OBSERVATION
Which units underperform. Which compositions are problematic. Which terrain is underutilized. Feeds into replay coaching for General-led battles.
ENGINE ARCHITECTURE — SIMULTANEOUS SYSTEMS
Pathfinding: Navigate terrain, avoid obstacles, seek optimal positions based on AI behavior.
Targeting: Priority rules — nearest, weakest, highest threat, commander designation.
Combat Resolution: Fire rate → accuracy roll (range, cover, Marks, Phase Blink) → damage (weapon type, armor, resistances).
Morale: Bio units track morale. Low morale = accuracy penalties, slower movement, routing. Machines/energy immune.
Special Mechanics: Field Repairs, Phase Blink, Wreckage Salvage, Reanimation, Marked Targets, Energy Absorption, Volatile Death.
Faction Overlays: Each mechanic runs as an overlay on core engine — consistent base, unique per faction.

GROUND COMBAT VISION
Dark Crusade + StarCraft + Mechabellum — The Blend
§19b.1 — Design Inspirations
Three Games · One System
DAWN OF WAR: DARK CRUSADE
Territory conquest map. Garrison defense. Attacker deploys from map edge. Buildings give defensive bonuses. Every territory is a place with meaning, not just a hex. The weight and permanence of conquest.
STARCRAFT
Unit composition and counter-play. Rock-paper-scissors dynamics. Positioning matters. The satisfaction of building the right army for the right fight. Visual readability at a glance.
MECHABELLUM
Auto-battler deployment. Formation strategy. Reserve waves. Player sets up, then watches with surgical intervention. The commander fantasy — preparation IS the skill expression.
§19b.2 — The Blend
How Each Contributes to Ground Combat
Pre-Battle: Deploy units in formation (Mechabellum) at a territory (Dark Crusade)
During Battle: Units auto-fight (Mechabellum) with counter-play mattering (StarCraft)
Terrain: Defender has building bonuses from territory (Dark Crusade)
Decisions: Player picks composition + formation + reserves, then watches. CP abilities for surgical intervention.
NON-NEGOTIABLE: AUTO-BATTLER STAYS
The auto-battler core is the foundation of the entire combat experience. Players do NOT directly control units. The skill expression is in preparation (80%) and intervention (20%). This is what makes Ashes of Command a strategy game, not a tactics game.
§19b.3 — Missing Pieces to Build
Systems Not Yet Implemented
1. Terrain & Cover
Units behind obstacles take less damage. Cover positions matter for deployment.
2. Defender Garrison Bonus
Buildings provide stat bonuses to defending units. Makes territory development directly impact combat.
3. Strategic Capture Points
Key points to capture during battle for tactical advantage. Encourages dynamic movement.
4. Flanking Bonus
Side/rear attacks deal more damage. Rewards positioning and formation depth.
THE EQUIPMENT SYSTEM
6 Slot Categories · 208 Items · 4 Rarity Tiers — Chapters 20-21
Every unit is a complete entity with its own identity. Customization comes from equipping weapons, armor, gear, ammunition, and modules. Equipment is acquired through research, battle loot, salvage, trade, and discovery. Higher-rank units unlock more slots.
The Six Slot Categories
Primary Weapon · Armor · Gear · Ammo · System · Special
[W] Primary Weapon
Main damage source. Found on all units.
[A] Armor Plating
HP bonus, damage resistance, special protection. All units.
[G] Gear
Tactical utility — grenades, scanners, repair kits. Infantry, Mechs. Locked at Rookie. Unlocks at Veteran.
[AM] Ammo Type
Modifies primary weapon damage type/behavior. Ranged, Vehicles, Ships.
[S] Synergy Module
Synergy equipment — targeting, sensors, ECM, engines. Vehicles, Air, Ships.
[SP] Special
Faction-unique or unit-unique signature equipment. Elite units only.

Rarity Tiers
Common · Uncommon · Rare · Legendary
COMMON

UNCOMMON

RARE

LEGENDARY
One-of-a-kind. Ancient Ruins, Guardian fragments. Cannot mass-produce. Game-changing.
Acquisition Channels
5 Ways to Get Equipment
Research (Tech Tree): Unlocks blueprints for mass production. Common + Uncommon.
Battle Loot (lootChance formula): Dropped by defeated enemies. Cross-faction possible. Uncommon + Rare.
Salvage: Post-battle scavenging (Horde is fastest). Common, occasionally Uncommon.
Trade (Black Market): Purchase with Scrap. Cross-faction items. Refreshes every 5 cycles. Uncommon + Rare.
Discovery: Ancient Ruins, Fallen Empires, Derelict Fleets. Rare + Legendary. The Keystone (+50% vs Guardians) = campaign-defining. One per campaign.
Tech Tree & Research (Ch28)
4–5 Tiers × 3–4 Branches Per Faction · 124 Nodes Total
SHARED STRUCTURE
Branch 1: Primary weapon mastery → Ultimate weapon tech
Branch 2: Defense & sustainability → Ultimate survivability
Branch 3: Logistics & command → Ultimate strategic tech
Branch 4: Special projects → Super-heavy, flagship, hybrid ammo
TIER PROGRESSION
T1: 2 cycles. Common unlocks. Available immediately.
T2 (a/b choice): 4 cycles. Uncommon. Requires T1.
T3: 6 cycles. Rare. Requires T2.
T4 (Culmination): 8 cycles. Game-changing. Requires T3.
RESEARCH SPEED MODIFIERS
Research Lab: Enables research (1 researcher)
Advanced Lab: +50% speed (2 researchers)
Ancient Ruins trait: -25% time in that system
Architect secondary: +10% speed
CROSS-FACTION TECH ADOPTION
Defeat enemies → 15% loot drop → Use but not produce → Build Xenotech Analysis Bay (20⚙, 4 cycles) → Reverse-engineer (3-5 cycles) → Blueprint permanently available. Late-game luxury, not standard strategy.

§21.3 — Commander Abilities REDESIGNED
Now Faction-Specific — General Rank 3+ Unlock
COMMANDER ABILITY SYSTEM — REDESIGNED
The old trait-based commander abilities (War Cry, Fortify, Rally, etc.) have been replaced by the faction-specific General Rank 3+ unlock system above. Each faction now has a unique commander-tier ability that unlocks when the assigned General reaches Rank 3, replacing the generic trait abilities.
See §21.1c faction tables — ability #5 in each faction is the General Rank 3+ unlock.
BUILDING-LOSS RULE
If a building that grants a CP ability is destroyed, the ability becomes LOCKED — unless another building of the same type exists elsewhere in the same system. This creates meaningful defensive decisions around protecting key infrastructure.
Example: Terran Orbital Defense destroyed → Precision Airstrike locked. But if a second Orbital Defense exists in another territory in the same system, the ability stays available.
FACTION CP MODIFIERS — RETIRED
The old shared faction modifier system (Terran +15% Orbital Strike, Shards +3s Energy Shield, etc.) has been retired. Faction-specific differences are now baked directly into each faction's unique ability set. Each faction has 6 completely distinct abilities with their own costs, effects, and unlock paths.
CHAIN OF COMMAND
Rank System · General AI Ego · Personality Traits · Standing Orders — Chapters 22-23
Units grow from anonymous Rookies to autonomous Generals through a kill-count promotion chain. At Elite rank they develop personality traits. At Commander they gain auras and CP abilities. At General they can command entire sectors and fleets independently — becoming characters in their own right, with goals, opinions, and defection risk.

Standing Orders
9 Orders · Personality Modifies Interpretation
EXPAND — Conquer neutral systems aggressively
DEFEND — Hold territory, engage only if attacked
FORTIFY — Build infrastructure, improve defenses
HARASS — Raid enemy supply, avoid big fights

General AI Ego System
Loyalty · Friction · Defection Arc
LOYALTY SCORE (0–100)
Gains: Victories, alignment with trait, respected orders, gifts of equipment, acknowledgment in Council.
Loses: Orders ignored, orders that contradict trait, excessive casualties under their command, rivals promoted over them.
<20 Loyalty: Friction events trigger. <5: Defection risk active.
FRICTION EVENTS
Disagreement: General pushes back in War Council. Requires player acknowledgment.
Insubordination: Modifies standing order 10-20% toward their trait preference.
Challenge: Demands resource, territory, or recognition — binary choice with consequences.
DEFECTION OUTCOMES BY TRAIT
Aggressive → Joins the faction you're currently at war with. Turns their tactical knowledge against you. · Cautious → Surrenders peacefully to nearest neutral faction. Takes their equipment but no violence. · Loyal → Vanishes heartbroken. Very rare. Returns as event during Final War. · Ambitious → Joins the strongest enemy faction. Accelerates their veteran production. · Reckless → Charges Vorax tendril or Guardian fleet alone. Dies heroically on their own terms. · Cunning → Goes fully independent. Becomes Pirate Warlord — minor faction on the galaxy map.
THE WAR COUNCIL & ADVISORS
15 Unique Characters (5 Factions × 3) · Doctrine Recommendations · Hidden Depths — Chapter 23
Convenes automatically: every 5 cycles, before Approach Phase, after major events (Vorax arrival, faction elimination, Guardian contact), and on loyalty warnings. Three advisors provide recommendations colored by their doctrine. Player listens, then decides. Every reaction is tracked. Nothing is neutral.
When the Council Convenes
6 Automatic Triggers — Never On-Demand
Every 5 Cycles
Strategic review. Advisors assess your territory, resources, and threat map.
Before Approach Phase
Each recommends War, Espionage, or Diplomacy for the upcoming system.
Vorax Arrival
Crisis session. Advisors disagree sharply on priority vs normal campaigns.
Faction Elimination
Post-mortem. Advisors assess what it means for the balance of power.
Guardian Contact
First encounter with Core Guardians. Vane speaks least. Valerius most alarmed.
Loyalty Warning
A General's loyalty falls below 30. Advisors recommend reconciliation or preemptive action.
The Three Advisors
Valerius · Krell · Vane — Three Doctrines, Three Hidden Depths
MAJOR VALERIUS — THE ARCHITECT
Calm, measured, speaks in probabilities and projections. Advocates patience, infrastructure, intelligence. At Approach Phase: always recommends Espionage first, Diplomacy second, War only as last resort.
Hidden Depth: Has a family on a sector he has mathematically calculated as "acceptable losses." His heart tells him otherwise. He never mentions it unless the player asks him directly — and even then, he deflects once before admitting. In the Terran Architect-aligned path, the Wake-Up recommendation during Final War comes from him — the canonical default.
GENERAL KRELL — THE VANGUARD
Rough, direct, speaks in absolutes and battlefield idioms. Advocates immediate aggression, overwhelming force, minimum hesitation. At Approach Phase: recommends War every time, without exception. Occasionally respected by enemy Generals.
Hidden Depth: Has an unbroken win record across hundreds of engagements. But the kill count accumulates behind his eyes. He advocates war not because he believes in it — it is simply the only language he knows how to speak. Rarely, very late in the campaign, he asks: "Was any of it worth it?"
INQUISITOR VANE — THE TYRANT
Quiet, deliberate, speaks entirely in implications and questions that are really statements. Advocates espionage, manufactured fear, population control, strategic cruelty. At Approach Phase: recommends Sabotage. Always.
Hidden Depth: Was an idealist. Brilliant, naive, full of hope. A single crisis event early in her career broke something that never healed. Not evil — TERRIFIED. Believes cruelty is the only effective deterrent in a universe that punishes mercy. The most dangerous person on the command deck — because she is not wrong about the galaxy, only about herself.
Approach Phase Recommendations
Each Advisor Has a Preferred Path
Advisor1st ChoiceContext Exceptions
Valerius Espionage Pushes Diplomacy if player has Intel < 8. Recommends War only if Guardian threat imminent.
Krell War Always War. If player has already been at war with the target for 5+ cycles, he suggests "crushing blow" variant.
Vane Sabotage Pushes for Sabotage + Diplomacy (false flag) combo when Influence > 15 and Intel > 10.
Simulation → Final War Reveal
The Twist That Recontextualizes Everything
During the simulation, advisors feel like AI constructs — program voices, support functions. The player assumes they are algorithms. Their recommendations feel like generated output. Their secrets feel like backstory flavor.
In the Final War: they are real people. Faces. Physical presence. Trembling hands. Personal stakes. Everything they said throughout the campaign was sincere — not playing roles, but teaching. Preparing. Warning. The player now understands every piece of advice they ignored.
Estimated dialogue: 50–80 lines each during simulation · 100–150 lines each during Final War. The Wake-Up recommendation is delivered by whichever advisor has the best relationship with the Commander — earned, not scripted. Valerius is the canonical/trailer default (Terran Architect-aligned).

All three advisors are members of whichever faction the player chose. Their doctrinal differences represent real political fault lines WITHIN that faction. Every faction has hawks, doves, and shadows. The GDD names (Valerius, Krell, Vane) are the Terran League set — the canonical default trio. Other 12 names TBD in Phase 3.

The Twist Hits Differently Per Faction

Advisor Inter-Relationships
The Triangle That Shifts With Alignment
The three advisors were selected/assigned TOGETHER — they have history before the Commander existed. They argue, defend, and undermine each other based on which doctrine the Commander favors. This makes the war council feel ALIVE.
ARCHITECT ↔ VANGUARD
Grudging mutual respect. Disagree on everything but recognize competence.
ARCHITECT ↔ TYRANT
Intellectual tension. Both strategic thinkers — one builds, the other breaks.
VANGUARD ↔ TYRANT
Most friction. The soldier despises manipulation. The manipulator sees a blunt instrument.
HOW ALIGNMENT SHIFTS THE TRIANGLE
ALIGNMENTFAVOREDOTHER TWO
ArchitectArchitect gains confidence, speaks freelyVanguard + Tyrant bond over frustration — “we’re being ignored”
VanguardVanguard emboldened, speaks louderArchitect grows quiet. Tyrant tries to USE the aggression.
TyrantTyrant opens up, almost warmArchitect + Vanguard ally against Tyrant path — united by fear.
BalancedNo one dominatesRichest dialogue. Three-way arguments. Most nuanced path.
The Wake-Up Moment
The Most Important Narrative Beat — Earned, Not Scripted
“Leave the simulation. The real war is here.” — delivered by whichever advisor has the best relationship with the Commander.
Tyrant advisor: “This training ground has taught you everything it can. The real galaxy is burning. You know what must be done.”
Vanguard advisor: “We’ve run enough drills. People are dying out there. REAL people. It’s time.”
Architect advisor: “The metrics suggest readiness. But readiness isn’t the point anymore. They need you.”
Balanced path: ALL THREE deliver it together. Rare moment of unity — three people who disagree on everything, agreeing on this one thing.
Advisor Death
The Sidelined Advisor Is At Risk
The advisor you ignored most takes a desperate risk in the Final War to prove they matter.
Some Relationship Maintained: They survive. Redemption moment. They earn their place.
Completely Neglected: They die. Underprepared, desperate, trying to matter. Your NEGLECT killed them, not the enemy.
Aftermath: Favored advisor feels guilt (“I should have included them”). Middle advisor feels anger (“You never listened to them. Not once.”). Hidden depth revealed posthumously.
Balanced/Unifier path is safest for keeping all three alive. Tyrant path is most dangerous — Architect advisor almost always at risk.
Advisors & The Strategist
Gradual Awareness — They Can’t Hear It, But They See the Changes
Early: Commander acts on hunches. Advisors chalk it up to intuition. “Good instinct, Commander.”
Mid: Commander references impossible intelligence. Pauses, listening to something invisible. Advisors notice.
Architect: “Your sources are unusually thorough. Where is this intelligence coming from?”
Vanguard: “Whatever’s in your head, keep it together.”
Tyrant: “Something is influencing you. I need to know what. Now.”
Late: Undeniable. Each responds per doctrine — Architect fascinated, Vanguard tolerant (“if it helps us win”), Tyrant threatened (another voice is competition).
Final War: All three have a relationship with the Strategist by proxy. The Strategist has opinions about THEM too — shares only if asked.
ADVISORS & THE AETHYN TRUTH — SHARED REVELATION
They learn WITH the Commander — no information asymmetry. Each processes through their doctrine lens:
Architect: “If all factions share a common ancestor… alliances aren’t just strategic. They’re reunification.”
Vanguard: “Doesn’t matter where we came from. What matters is who’s threatening us NOW.”
Tyrant: “If all factions are fragments of one species… whoever controls the Engine controls the WHOLE species.”

DESIGN NORTH STAR
“Write them so well that when the Final War reveal hits, the player pauses and sits in silence. Not because of a plot twist — because they realize they CARED about voices they assumed were algorithms.”

ESPIONAGE & DIPLOMACY
5 Operations · Diplomatic Actions · Economy · Events — Chapters 24, 26-27
Espionage Operations
Five Operation Types
Recon1 IntelReveals fleet composition, garrisons, buildings, planetary traits. Persists 5 cycles. Foundation for all other ops.
Deep Recon3 IntelRequires existing Recon. Reveals EXACT equipment loadouts, named Commanders + traits, victory conditions, hidden installations. The Approach Phase Espionage output.
Sabotage4 IntelTargets specific building for destruction. 60% base success (Sensor Spires −15% each). Failed = spy detected/captured, reputation penalty.
Counter-Intelligence2 IntelDeploy to friendly system. Persistent. 40%/cycle detection chance. Detected spies expelled (return in 2 cycles). Cunning Generals +20% detection.
Extraction3 IntelRescue captured spy. 40% success. Failed = BOTH agents lost (original executed). High-risk, high-reward.
ESPIONAGE VS VORAX
Standard ops don't work. Special ops:
Synapse Tracking (2I): Pre-battle map of Synapse positions.
Adaptation Analysis (3I): Reveals current mutation resistances + optimal weapon mix.
ESPIONAGE VS GUARDIANS
Standard ops don't work. Intel redirected to research:
Lore Fragment Discovery (4I): Cross-reference data to synthesize Guardian lore fragments. 1 per op. Repeatable every 5 cycles.

Commander Rescue Rules
Unit Destroyed — Two Possible Fates
BATTLE WON
Unit counts as wounded. Removed from field. Returns after 3 cycle recovery. All XP, traits, and equipment preserved. Terran bonus: Field Repair may prevent reaching 0 HP.
BATTLE LOST
Unit is captured or killed — fate determined by captor. Necro-Legion: interrogated, then reanimated as enemy. Vorax: consumed and assimilated. Guardians: vaporized on contact. Named units lost permanently = narrative event.
Slot Unlock Progression
Each Rank = +1 Equipment Slot · Terran Early Bonus
Rookies: [W] + [A] slots — the bare minimum. · Terran bonus: Veteran slot unlocked one rank early (at Rookie on Terran units). · General (all units): All 6 slots available. Equipment loadout becomes a full strategic layer.
THE DUAL THREAT MODEL
Ring + Wall = Funnel · Weapon Asymmetry — Chapter 31
VORAX = THE CLOSING RING (The Clock)
Expanding inward from the galaxy's edge. Consuming systems. Accelerating. THE TIMER. Cannot negotiate. Cannot coexist with. Only options: slow (destroy Tendrils) or stop permanently (activate Nexus). See §12.11 for Vorax spawn/movement prototype values.
GUARDIANS = THE WALL (The Destination)
Defending the galactic center. Stationary. Overwhelmingly powerful. Between you and the Nexus. Two approaches: fight through (Conquest Path — kinetic loadouts) or convince (Unification Path — 75% Compendium + 3+ alliances + negotiate the Warden).
WEAPON ASYMMETRY — THE CORE STRATEGIC DILEMMA
Anti-Vorax: Energy weapons (plasma, laser, ion). Kinetic works but doesn't exploit weakness. Biotic units resist energy.
Anti-Guardian: Kinetic weapons (railgun, ballistic). Energy weapons HEAL Guardian constructs — a hard counter that cannot be ignored.
The Dilemma: An army optimized for one threat is weak against the other. Three responses:
· Maintain two armies (expensive, complex)
· Re-equip between fronts (slow, risky if both active)
· Research Legendary hybrid weapons (late-game only — The Keystone)
The Funnel Structure
Ring Closes → Player Pushed Toward Guardian Wall
The galaxy map is deliberately designed so that as the Vorax ring closes inward, the only safe territory remaining is progressively closer to the galactic core — where the Guardians are strongest. The player can never simply avoid both threats indefinitely. The map architecture forces a confrontation with the wall while the clock is still running.
THE FINAL WAR — REALITY MODE
Permadeath · Procedural Destiny · Two Paths · Five Endings — Chapter 32
Begins after achieving Mastery in the simulation. A simulation-to-reality cutscene plays. A new galaxy generates from Procedural Destiny parameters seeded by the player's alignment across all previous runs. Archive bonuses carry over. Permadeath is now active — this is real.
Difficulty Modes
Three Permadeath Tiers
STORY
No permadeath. Full narrative accessible. All endings reachable.
STANDARD
Permadeath active. Unlimited saves. Archive bonuses apply.
HARDCORE
Permadeath. Ironman saves only. No Account bonuses.
Two Paths to the Nexus
Conquest or Unification — A Third Hybrid Exists
Path of Conquest
Military siege of Guardian constructs. Kinetic loadouts. The Keystone (+50% vs Guardians). Accept Volatile Death chain-reaction casualties as the price of victory.
Path of Unification
Coalition. Requires 75% Guardian Compendium completion + 3+ active alliances + max Influence + negotiate the Warden-Commander directly.
Pragmatist Hybrid
Fight through the first Guardian construct to demonstrate strength, then negotiate from that position. Unlocks unique dialogue branch with the Warden.

Canonical System IDs
WIN CONDITION
Conquer The Nexus (sys-nexus) → all Vorax nodes purged → VICTORY. Either by military force or negotiated activation.
LOSS CONDITION
Faction loses ALL controlled planets AND has no fleets in transit → faction eliminated. Archive SD awarded for battles won before the end.
The Five Endings
Alignment Determines the Galaxy's Fate
ARCHITECT: "The Ordered Galaxy"
Nexus imposes permanent cooperative resonance across all species. Galaxy is safe — but freedom is sacrificed to the system. 2-3 min cinematic if Architect is dominant alignment.
VANGUARD: "The Scorched Galaxy"
Nexus activated at maximum power. Vorax annihilated — but the galaxy is devastated in the process. Survival through total destruction. Shorter cinematic. Krell approves.
TYRANT: "The Iron Throne"
Commander seizes Nexus power. Vorax subjugated. Galaxy ruled as galactic deity. Order through dominance. The ending Vane has always believed was inevitable.
PYRRHIC VICTORY
Victory at catastrophic cost. The galaxy is saved — but your army is destroyed, your Generals dead, your civilization shattered. Rebuilt from nothing. Can trigger from any alignment path when losses exceed a threshold. Distinct cinematic — the weight of what was sacrificed.
UNIFIER (SECRET): "The Resonance"
Complete lore + complete alliances reverse the species-split. Galaxy healed. Vorax sealed permanently. Warp lanes reopened. The TRUE ending. Always the longest cinematic. Requires: balanced alignment + complete Unification negotiation + full Artifact chain. Full Guardian restoration. Reveals the Strategist’s true name. Valerius weeps.
