THE AI DIRECTOR
Procedural Narrative Engine · 42 Features · Baked-In Intelligence — Chapter 43
DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
"Every playthrough tells a different story — not because it's random, but because the galaxy is paying attention."
Architecture
What the AI Director Is (and Isn't)
The AI Director is a baked-in, offline procedural narrative engine. No LLM. No internet. No cloud processing. It runs on deterministic systems with weighted randomization, event templates with variable slots, faction personality matrices, and Markov chains for dialogue variation. It works on "a potato" — every calculation is local, every outcome reproducible with the same seed (geography-deterministic; player-reactive events vary by behavior).
EVENT TEMPLATES
Pre-written narrative structures with variable slots filled by game state. "General [NAME] held [SYSTEM] for [N] rounds. [CASUALTIES] survived." — never the same twice.
PERSONALITY MATRICES
Every General, commander, and advisor has personality weights (Aggressive/Cautious/Loyal/Ambitious) that determine dialogue selection, tactical preference, and relationship evolution.
MARKOV CHAINS
Dialogue variation engine. Template pools per personality type, assembled with controlled randomization. Consistent character voice, variable specific words. Deterministic with seeds.
Narrative Systems (8 Features)
The Galaxy Remembers Everything
RIVALRY ENGINE — CROSS-FACTION RELATIONSHIPS
Tracks relationships between YOUR commanders and ENEMY commanders through repeated encounters. Can be hostile or friendly. Five relationship types:

Bitter Nemesis: Multiple losses to same enemy. Morale penalty on their field, bonus damage against their forces.
Grudging Respect: Evenly matched. Back-and-forth victories. Neutral morale, acknowledgment dialogue.
Friendly Rival: Honorable repeated engagements. Easier diplomacy with that faction. Potential Final War defection/intel.
Blood Feud: Named veteran killed. Permanent aggression modifier. No negotiation through this commander.
Hunter/Prey: One-sided dominance. Enemy avoids your General's sector. Overconfidence risk if enemy adapts.

Vorax: No rivalries (swarm). Generals develop "Vorax Specialist" tags instead.
Guardians: One-sided until The Negotiation.

Does NOT modify internal Loyalty Score (0–100 system untouched). Affects combat modifiers, diplomacy options, and generated dialogue.
WAR CORRESPONDENT
Auto-generated after-action reports written into the Compendium. Not "you won" — "The 3rd Terran Armored held the ridge for 14 rounds. 4 survived." Pulls actual battle data: unit names, round counts, casualties, decisive moments. Procedural military journalism that makes every battle feel documented and real.
FACTION MEMORY
AI factions remember what you did to them. Burned an Accord colony? Their diplomats reference it 20 turns later. Spared a Shards fleet? They remember the mercy. Long-term grudge/gratitude tracking that makes every diplomatic interaction informed by history. Factions are not goldfish — they are civilizations with institutional memory.
ADVISOR MOOD SYSTEM
Valerius, Krell, and Vane (and their faction equivalents) gradually shift tone based on alignment drift. An Architect advisor watching you lean Tyrant doesn't snap — they slowly become colder, more formal, more distant. A Vanguard advisor watching you embrace their doctrine becomes warmer, more personal. Subtle tonal shifts across dozens of interactions, not binary mood switches.
UNIFIED CASCADE EVENT SYSTEM
Cosmic events (Nebula Surge, Gravitational Pulse, Meteor Shower, Pulsar Flare, Wormhole Resonance, Ion Storms) keep their existing timer values as defaults but now serve as first dominoes in cause-effect chains. The AI director chains political/economic consequences from cosmic triggers.

Example chain: Pulsar Flare → electronics disabled in adjacent system → supply route severed → garrison morale drops → border system vulnerability → Horde AI detects weakness and launches opportunistic raid → your fleet is out of position because of the Gravitational Pulse that fired 3 cycles ago.

Cosmic events are weather. Cascades are the politics that weather creates. One system, not two.
DIPLOMATIC INCIDENTS
NPC factions have their own relationships and wars. The Shards and the Accord might go to war over a border system — without your involvement. You can exploit the distraction, mediate for influence, or stay out of it entirely. The galaxy has politics even when you're not looking.
CULTURAL DRIFT
Long-held planets adopt faction traits over time. A Terran world held by the Accord for 30 cycles starts generating hybrid events — Terran citizens adopting Accord governance, resistance cells, cultural fusion that creates unique narrative moments. Occupation isn't just a flag change.
WHISPER NETWORK
Incomplete intelligence fragments based on espionage investment. You don't get "The Horde is attacking System Kepler-7." You get "Horde fleet movements detected near Kepler sector." Or "Intercepted transmission: '...the big push is...[garbled]...third cycle...'" Higher espionage investment = clearer fragments. The fog of war applies to information, not just territory.
Combat Flavor (4 Features)
Battles That Tell Stories
BATTLE CHATTER
Text popups generated from battle state. Units under fire call for support. Flanking units report success. Dying units leave last words. Pulled from personality-tagged template pools — a Cautious General's troops say different things than an Aggressive General's troops.
LAST STAND MOMENTS
When high-rank units die, the game generates rank/history-based death scenes. A Veteran who survived 12 battles doesn't just disappear — "Sergeant Voss held the line until the ammunition ran out. Then he held it with his hands." Written into the Compendium permanently.
POST-BATTLE SCARS
Procedural veteran flavor text with stat effects. A unit that survived a Vorax encounter might gain "Swarm Survivor: +10% vs Vorax, -5% morale in contested systems." Battle history becomes mechanical identity. Units that fought together develop bonds. Veterans carry their war.
ENEMY TAUNTS
Personality/history-based pre-battle messages from enemy commanders. A Bitter Nemesis sends threats. A Friendly Rival sends warnings. A Hunter sends nothing — silence is the taunt. Pulled from the Rivalry Engine relationship data and the commander's personality matrix.
Political Systems (2 Features)
Factions Are Not Monoliths
FACTION CIVIL WARS
AI factions aren't monoliths. Internal power struggles generate coups, splinter groups, defectors. A Necro-Legion subfaction reactivates with different protocols and breaks away. An Accord caste challenges the Supreme Commander's authority. You can exploit these fractures — or they can exploit yours.
TRADE ROUTE POLITICS
Trade routes are political leverage. Cutting supply to an enemy system through trade manipulation is quieter than an invasion and sometimes more effective. Trade agreements create dependencies — and dependencies create vulnerabilities.
Character Depth (4 Features)
People, Not Units
GENERAL JOURNALS → COMPENDIUM DOSSIERS
AI director generates journal-style entries that populate Commander Dossiers in the Compendium. No separate journal UI — the Dossier IS the journal. Military record mixed with personal voice. Open a General's Dossier and see stats, battle history, AND personality — all from one system.
MENTOR CHAINS
When a veteran General trains a rookie, the rookie inherits personality traces. Kill the mentor and the student's dialogue shifts — anger, grief, determination to live up to the legacy. Emergent lineages across campaigns.
DEFECTOR STORIES
When units or commanders defect (from loyalty failure or diplomatic events), they bring story with them. A defecting Accord commander explains WHY they left. Their former faction sends messages — threats, pleas, or silence. Defection is a narrative event, not just a faction swap.
BETRAYAL FORESHADOWING
Before a General betrays you (loyalty collapse), there are signs. Missed orders explained away. Reports that don't quite add up. A subtle shift in dialogue tone. The AI director plants foreshadowing 5-10 cycles before the betrayal. Observant players can catch it. Most won't — until the second playthrough.
Environmental Storytelling (4 Features)
The Galaxy's Scars
RUINS TELL STORIES
Pre-Fracture ruins discovered during expansion contain procedurally assembled lore fragments. Each ruin has a story template filled with Aethyn history, Fracture details, or faction origins. Discovering multiple ruins in sequence can piece together larger narratives. Feeds Compendium entries and unlocks Negotiation dialogue options.
GHOST STATIONS
Abandoned stations with automated distress signals still broadcasting. Board them for resources, technology fragments, or lore. Some are traps. Some contain AI still following orders from civilizations that no longer exist. Each one is a micro-story about what happened when the Fracture hit.
DERELICT FLEETS
Fleets that died mid-transit during the Fracture, still drifting in formation. Salvageable for resources. Some contain commander logs. Some contain prototype equipment from pre-Fracture tech that no faction has rediscovered. Encounter type varies by location — Core-adjacent derelicts are Aethyn. Outer rim derelicts are early faction attempts at expansion that failed.
ANCIENT BATTLEFIELD SITES
Locations where major battles occurred during or after the Fracture. Wreckage fields with salvage bonuses. Sensor ghosts from old engagements. Occasionally, Necro-Legion units reactivating from battlefield remains — were they always here, or did someone wake them?
Sound & Atmosphere (3 Features)
What You Hear Matters
ADAPTIVE SOUNDTRACK
Music layers respond to game state. Peaceful exploration has ambient layers. Approaching Vorax territory adds tension. Combat escalates. Near-defeat strips to a single instrument. Victory swells. The AI director controls music intensity as a narrative tool.
ENVIRONMENTAL AUDIO
Faction-specific ambient audio when viewing their territory. Terran systems hum with industry. Shards systems shimmer with crystal resonance. Horde systems rattle and grind. Vorax territory... pulses. Biological. Wrong. The sound design tells you whose space you're in before you read the label.
SILENCE AS DESIGN
Consumed Vorax worlds have no sound. No ambient audio. No music. Nothing. After hours of rich soundscape, the absence is deafening. Silence is the most disturbing sound effect in the game. Post-consumption worlds are dead — and they sound like it.
Metagame & Cross-Run (3 Features)
The Simulation Remembers
GHOST FLEETS
In subsequent simulation runs, you occasionally encounter "echo" fleets in positions where you placed fleets in previous runs. They aren't real — they're the Crucible testing whether you'll repeat patterns. Defeating your own ghosts teaches the simulation that you've evolved. Ties into Archive persistence layer (Ch 33).
CRUCIBLE MEMORY
The simulation tracks broad strategic patterns across runs. Relied on choke points last time? They're less advantageous this time — enemy AI avoids them or the galaxy generates fewer of them. The Crucible isn't cheating — it's training you. Each run, the galaxy adapts to what worked before, forcing you to evolve. Aligns with Procedural Destiny (Ch 3).
SEED SHARING
Galaxy seeds are shareable — same seed produces same geography, same faction placements, same static hazard positions. Player-reactive events (cascades, Vorax adaptation, rivalries) vary by behavior, so two players with the same seed get the same MAP but different STORIES. Geography-deterministic, narrative-reactive.
Vorax-Specific (4 Features)
The Swarm Evolves
FULL ADAPTIVE SWARM TACTICS
ALL Vorax parameters are available to the AI director: spawn timing, movement speed, force composition, and targeting priority. Current values (Cycle 6 spawn, 1 hop/cycle, 10 cycle respawn) serve as defaults the AI director can modify based on player behavior. Fortify the east? Next Tendril hits from the south. Go mobile? They mass up. Rely on armor? Acid-spitter compositions shift to melt it. The Deep Hive Mind is ancient and strategic — it doesn't move faster, it moves smarter.
TENDRIL PERSONALITIES
Each Vorax Tendril has behavioral variation generated by the AI director. One Tendril is aggressive and direct. Another is cautious, probing, pulling back when it meets resistance. A third targets infrastructure exclusively — ignoring fleets to eat your supply lines. The hive mind isn't a single strategy. It's a portfolio of approaches testing which one works against YOU.
CONSUMPTION AFTERMATH
Worlds consumed by Vorax aren't just "captured" — they're transformed. Short occupation = corrupted biosphere, partially recoverable. Long occupation = bare rock, no atmosphere, no resources. Engine purge = molecular erasure, the planet itself is smaller. The visual and mechanical degradation of consumed worlds tells the story of what the Vorax are — hunger doesn't leave ruins, it leaves husks.
TIERED EVOLUTION EVENTS
Two-layer evolution system:

Minor (Mid-Campaign, Visible): Gradual cosmetic + small stat shifts as Vorax consume territory. A Tendril that ate Terran worlds visibly gains armor plating over multiple cycles. Slow enough to react. The horror of watching them become your weapons turned against you.

Major (Per-Encounter, Surprise): Significant ability absorption revealed only when you next fight them. "They have PHASE BLINK now?!" — a Tendril that consumed Shards space gained their signature ability. The Deep Hive Mind pushes strategic evolution down from above.

Tendril-level learning = gradual. Deep Hive Mind strategic evolution = between fights. Starvation resets Tendril adaptations but not Deep Hive Mind memory.
Guardian-Specific (4 Features)
The Ancient Watchers
DEGRADATION SPECTRUM
Guardian behavior varies by corruption level. Clean units (Bastion) are precise and rational. Moderately degraded units exhibit strange patterns — repetitive patrol routes, scanning objects that aren't there. Severely corrupted units (The Veil) are hostile, unpredictable, and may attack other Guardians. The AI director selects from different behavior pools based on each unit's corruption state.
OUTPOST ENCOUNTERS
Automated Guardian outposts along the Shattered Expanse approach and rare lost units drifting in the wider galaxy. Each encounter is procedurally flavored — some are hostile (degraded, shoot first), some are communicative (partial data exchanges), some are mysteries (what is this unit doing so far from Core?). Research data source for Compendium entries.
THE NEGOTIATION — ENDGAME DIPLOMATIC ENCOUNTER
Three-phase diplomatic encounter with the Warden-Commander at the Nexus. Not a quiz — a conversation between two intelligences shaped by everything the player has done.

Phase 1 — Grievances: The Warden-Commander confronts you with actual campaign data. "You burned 14 worlds." "You enslaved three of my outpost garrisons." Your responses depend on alignment AND Compendium knowledge. Deep knowledge unlocks nuanced diplomatic responses. Without it, you're arguing blind.

Phase 2 — Understanding: Philosophical challenges based on discovered Compendium entries. "The Engine can restore the warp lanes. It can also weaponize them. Which would you do?" If you've found Strategist fragments, you can recontextualize the Warden-Commander's millennia of guilt — its failure was DESIGNED. The Strategist needed the factions to evolve independently.

Phase 3 — Terms: Path-dependent negotiation. Unifier = alliance with conditions (Guardian autonomy, representation, joint restoration). Architect = knowledge access under oversight. Vanguard = military constraints negotiation. Tyrant = confrontation/combat (no negotiation, lose Engine expertise).

Warden-Commander personality varies by entry point: Bastion = calm, The Veil = hostile, The Garden = gentle. Compendium entries unlock dialogue options, not quiz answers. Negotiation "temperature" tracked — push too hard and the door closes, too passive and respect is lost.
GUARDIAN MEMORY
The Guardians have been watching the galaxy for millennia. They know things. If you build trust (through outpost encounters, careful approach to Core, Strategist fragment collection), they share fragments of pre-Fracture history. Not freely — grudgingly, testing whether you'll use the knowledge well. The oldest functioning Guardian has memories of the Aethyn themselves. Finding it is a quest. Earning its trust is a campaign.
Simulation Layer (3 Features)
Cracks in the Crucible
SIMULATION GLITCHES
Subtle foreshadowing of the Crucible's true nature. A star that flickers like a rendering artifact. A unit that clips through terrain for one frame. Textures that briefly show grid lines. Not bugs — breadcrumbs. The AI director places 3-5 per simulation run, increasing in frequency as the player approaches the truth. Players who notice them are already asking the right questions.
STRATEGIST ECHOES
The Original Strategist's personality bleeding through the simulation. Odd turns of phrase in advisor dialogue that don't match their character. A battle report that reads like it was written by someone ancient. The Strategist isn't communicating — it's LEAKING. The simulation was built from its mind, and sometimes the seams show.
ADAPTIVE DIFFICULTY WITHOUT NUMBERS
The AI director adjusts challenge through BEHAVIOR, not stat scaling. Winning too easily? Enemy commanders play smarter — flanking, feinting, retreating to regroup. Struggling? They make tactical errors — overextending, splitting forces, ignoring flanks. No invisible health buffs. No damage multipliers. The enemies just think differently. The player never feels cheated because nothing was inflated — the opponents just adapted.
The Big One
The Crucible Learns
THE CRUCIBLE LEARNS — CROSS-RUN STRATEGIC ADAPTATION
Each simulation run tracks the player's strategic patterns: preferred fleet compositions, favored expansion directions, alliance tendencies, combat timing. The next run, the galaxy adapts. Horde repositioned to counter your expansion route. Accord more aggressive on your weak flank. Vorax Tendrils hitting where you historically leave gaps.

The simulation literally trains the player. You cannot win the same way twice. The Crucible is an Ender's Game battle room that watched every fight you've ever had and designed the next one to break your habits.

The in-lore justification: The Strategist built the Crucible to produce a leader capable of saving the galaxy. Not a leader who can win ONE scenario — a leader who can adapt to ANYTHING. Every failed run teaches the Crucible what you can handle. Every successful run raises the bar. The simulation isn't your enemy. It's your teacher. And it's the most patient teacher in the universe — it's been running for millennia, waiting for someone who can graduate.

Integrates with: Archive persistence (Ch 33), Procedural Destiny (Ch 3), Ghost Fleets, Crucible Memory. Scope: behavior tracking + weighted adjustments to galaxy generation and AI personality selection. No stat inflation — smarter opponents, harder scenarios, evolved challenges.
FEATURES CUT (5)
The following were evaluated and cut during design review: Propaganda Engine (scope creep), Refugee Flows (too much simulation overhead), Puppet States (overlaps with diplomacy system), Commander Legacy (cross-run identity conflicts with fresh starts), The Watcher (redundant with Crucible Learns).

L.4 Dynamic BattleManager Architecture (Godot 4.4)
Config-driven battle orchestrator. Accepts army composition via start_battle(config: Dictionary). Handles variable army sizes, dynamic formation placement, reserve wave reinforcements, and last-stand mechanics.
KEY FILES
BattleManager.gd — Orchestrator (spawn, reserves, victory)
BattleUnit.gd — Per-unit AI (target, move, attack, death)
BattleHUD.gd — HUD (counts, timer, speed controls)
BattleCamera.gd — Auto-track camera system
BattleArena.tscn — Scene root (ground, zones, lighting)
FORMATION CONSTANTS
UNIT_SPACING 2.5m — between units in row
ROW_GAP 3.5m — between front/back rows
TEAM_OFFSET_X 8.0m — distance from center
MAX_PER_ROW 5 — wrap threshold

L.4.2 Reserve Wave System
RESERVE DEPLOYMENT
Reserves defined per-team in battle config
Each wave: unit_id, count, deploy_delay (seconds)
Spawns at team back edge (TEAM_OFFSET_X + 6.0m)
1.0s spawn protection (immune + fade-in tween)
HUD notification with 2s display + 1s fade
LAST-STAND MECHANIC
If all field units die but reserves remain:
→ Force-deploy ALL pending reserves immediately
Prevents instant-loss when reinforcements are queued
Victory deferred until force-deploy resolves
Outcomes: PLAYER WINS / ENEMY WINS / DRAW
L.5 Battle Pipeline — 11-Step Combat Formula
#OPERATIONFORMULA
1Accuracy Rollrand() < attacker.accuracy → hit or miss
2Base Damageattacker.attack_damage
3Critical Hitrand() < crit_chance → dmg × crit_multiplier
4Evasion Rollrand() < target.evasion → attack dodged
5Resistancedmg × (1.0 − target.resistances[dmg_type])
6Armor Reductiondmg = max(1, dmg − target.armor)
7Damage Floormax(1, final_dmg) — always at least 1
8Shield Absorbshield absorbs first; overflow → HP
9HP Deductiontarget.current_hp −= remaining_dmg
10Death Checkhp ≤ 0 → emit unit_died, disable, death FX
11Floating NumberDamageNumber3D at target pos (crit = yellow)

L.6 Runtime Bugs Found & Fixed During Godot Testing
#BUG / RESOLUTION
1modulate not declared on CharacterBody3D
Symptom: Runtime error — modulate property not found on BattleUnit (CharacterBody3D).
Cause: modulate is a CanvasItem property (2D only). BattleUnit extends CharacterBody3D (3D).
Fix: Replaced with GeometryInstance3D.transparency. Added recursive _set_mesh_transparency(node, value). Spawn protection tweens 0.7 → 0.0.
File: Scripts/Systems/BattleUnit.gd
2Invalid access to is_alive on previously freed instance
Symptom: Crash after first unit death — accessing .is_alive on a freed BattleUnit reference.
Cause: Death tween calls queue_free(), but player_units / enemy_units arrays still hold stale references.
Fix: Added is_instance_valid(u) guards at all 9 access points across BattleManager.gd (6) and BattleUnit.gd (3).
Files: Scripts/Managers/BattleManager.gd, Scripts/Systems/BattleUnit.gd
3filter() lambda type-cast crash on freed objects
Symptom: Victory filters return empty arrays — instant DRAW after first death.
Cause: Typed lambda func(u: BattleUnit) — GDScript casts argument before lambda body runs. Freed object fails cast before is_instance_valid() can help.
Fix: Removed type hints: func(u) instead of func(u: BattleUnit). Changed result arrays to untyped Array.
File: Scripts/Managers/BattleManager.gd (lines 366, 369)
4Integer division warning in timer display
Symptom: Godot console warning on int / int truncation.
Cause: int(battle_time) / 60 performs integer division, flagged by GDScript 4.x.
Fix: Changed to int(battle_time / 60.0) — float division first, then explicit truncation.
File: UI/Screens/BattleHUD.gd (line 51)
L.7 Godot 4.4 Engine Gotchas (Cumulative)
#GOTCHADETAIL / WORKAROUND
1class_name on Autoload scriptsCauses naming conflict — don't use on GameDatabase.gd
2const Dict with Color() constructorsMay not compile — use var instead of const
3Array[TypedClass] can't hold freed refsTyped arrays reject freed objects. Use untyped Array when elements may be freed mid-frame.
4Typed lambda params crash on freed refsfunc(u: BattleUnit) casts before body runs. Freed object fails cast. Use func(u) untyped.
5modulate is CanvasItem only (2D)Use GeometryInstance3D.transparency for 3D fade effects.
6queue_free() doesn't null array refsAlways guard with is_instance_valid() at every access point, or remove from arrays on death.
7.glb models require editor importAutomatic on project open — wait for import to complete before running scenes.
8exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0)Illegal in Web Audio — use 0.0001 instead of 0.
9e.target.closest() on text nodesCan fail — guard with inline fallback: (e.target.closest ? e.target : {closest:()=>null})
10HP bars: QuadMesh billboardUnshaded, no_depth_test, billboard via camera basis copy, left-anchor drain, alpha 0.7.

L.9 Procedural Galaxy Generation: Implementation Specification
L.9.1 Galaxy Size Parameters
SIZESYSTEMSNEUTRALCYCLES/RUNNOTES
Small12 – 146 – 820 – 30Tight, early conflict inevitable
Medium16 – 2010 – 1430 – 45Standard balanced experience

Nexus always placed + 2–5 faction homeworlds based on custom difficulty settings.
System count stays the same regardless of faction count — fewer factions = more neutral systems to contest.
L.9.2 Fixed Anchor & Faction Homeworlds
ANCHORIDPOSITIONRULES
The Nexussys-nexus(510, 320) fixedWin condition target. Guardian fleet: Gunship×2 + Dreadnought. Connected by 2–3 lanes.
FACTION HOMEWORLDS (Procedurally Placed)
FACTIONHOMEWORLDPLACEMENT RULETOGGLEABLE
Terran LeagueProcedural nameOuter rim, spread from other homeworldsNO
Eternal ShardsProcedural nameOuter/mid rim, spread from other homeworldsYES
Scrap-HordeProcedural nameOuter rim, spread from other homeworldsYES
Necro-LegionProcedural nameMid/inner rim, spread from other homeworldsYES
Unity AccordProcedural nameOuter/mid rim, spread from other homeworldsYES
Custom Difficulty: Player can toggle AI factions on/off before galaxy generation. Minimum 2 factions (player + 1 AI). Fewer factions = more neutral systems. Vorax (NPC) and Core Guardians (NPC) always present regardless of toggle.
Homeworld Rules: Each homeworld is a normal procedural system — no fixed coordinates. Must be ≥3 lane-hops apart from each other. No homeworld can have a direct lane to the Nexus. Each homeworld gets a guaranteed Capital World planet.
Faction Elimination: A faction is destroyed when it loses ALL controlled planets AND has no fleets in transit. If a fleet is still moving, the faction survives.
L.9.3 Generation Pipeline (13 Steps)
#STEPSPECIFICATION
1Seed InitializationAccept seed (user-provided or time-based). Init seeded PRNG (mulberry32). All randomness flows through this.
2System CountPick random count within size range (S:12–14, M:16–20, L:22–26, X:28–35). Fewer active factions = more neutral systems (count stays the same).
3Place Nexus + HomeworldsNexus at (510, 320). Place N faction homeworlds (N = active factions, 2–5) via spaced radial placement: ~360°/N apart ±jitter, radius 0.65–0.90 × galaxy_radius. Each gets a guaranteed Capital World. Enforce ≥3 lane-hop separation.
4Generate SystemsPlace remaining (total − 1 − N) systems via jittered radial placement on 1024×640 space. Min distance 80px. Inner ring (0.2–0.4r): White Dwarf/Blue bias. Mid (0.4–0.7r): Yellow/Binary. Outer (0.7–1.0r): Red Giant/any.
5Assign Star Types5 types: Yellow Main Seq, Red Giant, Blue Supergiant, Binary, White Dwarf. Distribution biased by ring. Fisher-Yates shuffle of type pool.
6Generate PlanetsCount by star type (Yellow:5-8, Red:6-10, Blue:4-7, Binary:3-6, WD:2-5). Planet type weighted by star. Each gets: type, territory count, base yield, traits.
7Generate Warp LanesFor each system: connect to 2 nearest, 50% chance for 3rd. Dedupe edges. Ensure 1–3 chokepoints (prune longest edges).
7bRoll Orbital FeaturesFor each planet, filter ORBITAL_FEATURES by valid planet types, weighted pick. Keys: asteroid_belt, ring_system, debris_field, none.
8Post-Lane PruningRemove direct Homeworld↔Nexus lane for ALL factions. BFS flood fill. If disconnected subgraph found, add minimum bridge lane. Verify all homeworlds ≥3 lane-hops apart (re-add/remove lanes if needed).
9Place Wormholes1–2 pairs connecting non-adjacent systems (>60% galaxy diameter apart). Collapse chance: 5–40% per use, fixed per seed.
10Faction PlacementN homeworlds already placed in Step 3. Nexus = Guardians. Vorax at 1–2 edge systems (not homeworlds). Remaining systems = neutral/unoccupied. Elimination: all planets lost + no fleets in transit = destroyed.
11Assign Planet TraitsRoll from Ch13 tables: Resource (Rich Veins 20% Volcanic, Flux 15% Ocean), Combat (Fortified 15% Capital, Low-G 100% Moon), Strategic (Precursor 30% Ruins, Guardian Echo 15% Ruins/WD). Max 1 per category per planet.
12Territory AdjacencyPer planet: build connected territory graph (DoW Soulstorm style). Ring backbone 1→2→…→N→1 guarantees all reachable. Add 1–3 seeded cross-links for strategic shortcuts. Max 5 connections per territory. Store as adjacency dict { 1: [2, N], … }.
12bRoll System PhenomenaPer-system weighted pick. nebula, ion_storm, gravity_well, radiation_field, solar_flare_zone, none. Homeworlds always none. Nexus always gravity_well.
13OutputReturn { seed, size, systems[], lanes[], wormholes[], homeworlds{} }. Each system: { id, name, position, star_type, planets[], faction, is_homeworld, lanes[] }. Each planet: { type, territory_count, territory_adjacency{}, base_yield, traits[] }.
L.9.4 Seeded RNG Requirement
Same seed MUST produce identical galaxy across all platforms.
Implementation: mulberry32 seeded PRNG. All random calls routed through it.
Fisher-Yates shuffle for all randomized array selections.
Godot's built-in randi() not used — not guaranteed deterministic cross-platform.

L.10 — Living Universe: Orbital Mechanics & Galactic Phenomena
The galaxy is not a static game board. Every celestial body moves. Storms drift. Vorax tendrils creep. Players who study the rhythms gain a strategic edge.
GAMEPLAY WEIGHT: MODERATE — meaningful timing for big campaigns, not punishing for casual play.
L.10.1 — ORBITAL CYCLE SYSTEM
ORBITAL SLOTSPEED (°/CY)FULL ORBITNOTES
Slot 1 (innermost)30°12 cyclesFast, near the star
Slot 220°18 cycles 
Slot 314°~26 cycles 
Slot 410°36 cycles 
Slot 57°~51 cycles 
Slot 65°72 cycles 
Slot 7+ (outermost)3°120 cyclesSlow, far from star
System drift: 0.5°/cycle (720 cycles for full galactic orbit). Warp lane distances recalculate ±5% per cycle.
L.10.2 — TRAVEL TIME ORBITAL IMPACT
INTRA-SYSTEM
Base 1 cycle. −0.5 if planets within 60° (same side), +0.5 if >180° apart (opposite sides). Net: 0.5–1.5 cycles.
INTER-SYSTEM
current_distance / base_distance modifier (0.95–1.05). Displayed as Optimal / Standard / Extended.
LAUNCH WINDOWS
Open when two systems at closest approach. 15% travel discount, lasts 2–3 cycles, occurs every 30–50 cycles per lane. Shown as green pulse on warp lane.
L.10.3 — BATTLE CONDITION ORBITAL MODIFIERS
ORBITAL POSITIONEFFECTMODIFIER
Perihelion (closest)Intense heat/radiation+10% energy dmg, −5% bio HP regen
Aphelion (farthest)Cold/dark+10% stealth, −5% move speed
Mid-orbitStandardNo modifier
L.10.4 — CELESTIAL HAZARDS
PULSAR BEAMS
Rotating energy beams sweep nearby systems every 8–12 cycles. Fleets caught lose ALL shields for 2 cycles. Systems near pulsars +30% scrap yield. Visible as rotating lighthouse beam.
NEUTRON STAR GRAVITY WELLS
Fleet sublight speed HALVED. +50% scrap yield. Retreat from combat +2 cycles. Natural chokepoints.
SOLAR FLARES
Every 10–20 cycles by star type (Red:10, Yellow:15, Blue:20). Orbital structures disabled 1–2 cycles, unshielded fleets 5% hull dmg/cycle, ground battles +10% energy weapon damage. Predictable countdown.
L.10.5 — MOVING GALACTIC HAZARDS

L.10.6 — COSMIC OPPORTUNITIES
ROGUE PLANETS
1–2 per galaxy, drift ~1–2 u/cycle. Temporarily capturable for 5–8 cycles when near a system. Random type/traits. First to claim gets a bonus planet.
DEBRIS FIELDS
Dynamic — generated after major space battles. Persist 10–15 cycles. Salvageable for scrap + rare equipment. Ambush cover (first-strike bonus). Diminishing returns.
ANTIMATTER FOUNTAINS
1–2 per galaxy, stationary. Fleet parked 2 cycles = full shield + HP recharge. Strategically valuable control points.
L.10.7 — STAR SYSTEM PHENOMENA
TIDAL LOCKING
Inner planets around red giants/white dwarfs. Day side: +15% energy dmg, −10% bio regen. Night side: +15% kinetic dmg, −10% movement. Twilight zone: no modifiers. Visible per territory.
PLANETARY RING MINING
Gas giants with rings: +3 scrap/cycle for 20–30 cycles, then depleted. Rings thin visually when depleted.
BINARY STAR ECLIPSES
Every 15–25 cycles, lasting 2–3 cycles. All planets get night-side conditions (−10% ranged accuracy, +15% stealth). Predictable cycle in system info.

L.13 — DeploymentScene Architecture (Godot 4.4 Rewrite)
“Pre-battle force allocation — choose your initial wave and reserves before the fight begins.”
L.13.1 — SCENE TRANSITION PATTERN
Static var pending_battle_config — The DeploymentScene writes a static pending_battle_config dictionary before transitioning to BattleManager. BattleManager reads this config in _ready() and clears it after consumption. This avoids scene-to-scene parameter passing through globals.
Flow: MapScene → DeploymentScene (player allocates forces) → BattleManager (reads pending_battle_config) → Battle begins.
L.13.2 — THREE-COLUMN LAYOUT
AVAILABLEINITIAL WAVERESERVES
All player units eligible for this battleUnits deployed at battle startUnits held back, deployed later via reserve mechanic
L.13.3 — CLICK FLOW
ACTIONRESULT
Click unit in AvailableMoves to Initial Wave
Click unit in Initial WaveMoves to Reserves
Click unit in ReservesReturns to Available
L.13.4 — ENEMY TEAM GENERATION
Auto-generated enemy team mirrors the player’s composition. The enemy faction’s unit pool is filtered to match the player’s unit count and approximate tier distribution. This ensures balanced encounters without manual enemy roster design.
L.13.5 — CONFIG OUTPUT FORMAT
Output dictionary is compatible with BattleManager.start_battle(). Contains:
• player_initial: Array[UnitData]
• player_reserves: Array[UnitData]
• enemy_units: Array[UnitData]
• battle_type: String
• system_id: int
L.14 — Galaxy Map Visual Layer (Godot 4.4 Rewrite)
“Animated parallax starfield with nebula clouds — cosmetic layer that never touches galaxy generation.”
L.14.1 — 3-LAYER PARALLAX STARFIELD
LAYERCOUNTBEHAVIOUR
Far (back)200Smallest dots, slowest parallax scroll, subtle twinkle
Mid80Medium dots, moderate parallax, moderate twinkle
Near (front)30Largest dots, fastest parallax, strongest twinkle
L.14.2 — STAR TWINKLING
Sine wave modulation per star. Each star has a random phase offset and speed. Alpha oscillates between base_alpha × 0.5 and base_alpha × 1.0. Applied per-frame in _process(delta).
L.14.3 — NEBULA CLOUD PATCHES
2–4 soft nebula patches placed randomly across the map. Each patch is rendered as concentric circles with low alpha (0.01–0.03). Colors drawn from faction palette. Purely cosmetic — no gameplay effect.
L.14.4 — SEPARATE RNG
Visual layer uses a dedicated RNG with seed 42. This is completely separate from the galaxy generation RNG. Ensures that adding/removing visual elements never changes the procedurally generated galaxy layout.
L.14.5 — 11-LAYER DRAW PIPELINE (CC-011 OVERHAUL)
#LAYERDESCRIPTION
1Background Stars3-layer parallax starfield with twinkle
2Nebula CloudsSoft faction-colored patches with low alpha
3Galactic Core GlowConcentric warm gradient centered on Nexus
4Faction Influence ZonesSoft colored halos around faction-owned systems
5Warp LanesBase lane lines connecting systems
6Lane Pulse AnimationEnergy dots traveling along warp lanes
7Wormhole PortalsSpinning purple spirals at wormhole endpoints
8System NodesStar-type colored fill, faction ring, planet-count sizing
9Homeworld BeaconsPulsing rings + compass tick marks
10System LabelsSystem name text below each node
11Selection HighlightClick feedback ring on selected system
L.14.6 — GALACTIC CORE GLOW
Concentric warm gradient centered on the Nexus system (512, 320). Multiple circles radiate outward with decreasing alpha, blending from warm gold/amber at the center to transparent at the edges. Creates a visual “galactic core” focal point that draws the eye to the Nexus objective.
L.14.7 — SPIRAL ARM STAR CLUSTERING
Logarithmic spiral density applied to background star placement. Stars cluster along spiral arm paths radiating from the galactic center, creating a more natural galaxy appearance. Uses the visual RNG (seed 42) — does not affect game system placement.
L.14.8 — STAR-TYPE NODE COLORS
Each system node’s fill color reflects its star type (yellow for yellow_main_seq, red for red_giant, blue for blue_supergiant, white for white_dwarf, dual-tone for binary). An outer ring color indicates faction ownership. Unowned systems show a neutral grey ring.
L.14.9 — LANE PULSE ANIMATION
Energy dots travel along warp lanes at a steady pace. Multiple dots per lane, evenly spaced, animated each frame via _process(delta). Dot positions wrap at lane endpoints. Gives the galaxy a living, connected feel without impacting gameplay logic.
L.14.10 — WORMHOLE PORTALS
Spinning purple spirals rendered at each wormhole endpoint. Drawn as arcs that rotate over time, creating a swirling portal effect. Both ends of a wormhole pair display matching portals. Wormhole connections are drawn as dashed lines between paired systems.
L.14.11 — HOMEWORLD BEACONS
Pulsing rings + compass tick marks surround each faction’s homeworld system. The ring expands and contracts on a sine cycle, drawing attention to the faction’s capital. Four compass ticks (N/S/E/W) extend outward from the ring. Colored in the faction’s primary color.
L.14.12 — SYSTEM SIZE SCALING
System node radius scales by planet count. Systems with more planets render as larger circles on the galaxy map, providing an at-a-glance indication of system value. Homeworlds receive an additional size bonus to ensure they are always prominent.
L.14.13 — FACTION INFLUENCE ZONES
Soft colored halos drawn around faction-owned systems. Each faction’s influence zone uses that faction’s primary color at very low alpha, creating a territorial “fog” that visually groups owned systems. Overlapping zones blend naturally. Drawn on layer 4, below lanes and nodes.
L.15 — Turn Phase Pipeline Architecture (Godot 4.4 Rewrite)
“Full 6-phase turn cycle with adaptive phase skipping and conflict-driven resolution.”
L.15.1 — 6-PHASE CYCLE
#PHASEAUTO-DELAYDESCRIPTION
1MAP—Player input phase: issue fleet orders, manage units, review territory
2ARMADA0.5sExecute fleet moves, run conflict detection (multi-faction fleet presence)
3APPROACHskippablePre-battle fleet positioning (skipped if no conflicts)
4SPACE0.3sSpace combat resolution (skipped if no conflicts)
5GROUND0.3sGround combat resolution (skipped if no conflicts)
6RESOLUTION—Collect resources via supply chain, apply combat results, advance turn counter
L.15.2 — ADAPTIVE PHASE SKIPPING
The pipeline skips APPROACH, SPACE, and GROUND phases when no conflicts are detected during the ARMADA phase. Conflict detection checks for multi-faction fleet presence at any system. If no conflicts exist, the pipeline jumps directly from ARMADA to RESOLUTION, keeping peaceful turns fast.
L.15.3 — MVP CONFLICT RESOLUTION
In the MVP implementation, conflict resolution is simplified: the attacker captures one territory per conflict. Full space and ground battle scenes will be wired in later phases. This allows the turn pipeline to function end-to-end while battle mechanics are developed independently.
L.15.4 — RESOURCE COLLECTION (RESOLUTION PHASE)
During RESOLUTION, each faction collects yields from all owned territories. Yields are modified by the supply chain hop distance from homeworld (see §15.9). Credits, scrap, influence, and intel are accumulated per-territory and added to faction totals. The turn counter then advances and the pipeline returns to MAP.
L.15.5 — END TURN BUTTON STATES
PHASEBUTTON TEXTBEHAVIOUR
MAPEnd TurnClickable — commits player orders and starts phase execution
ARMADAExecuting…Disabled — fleet moves processing
SPACE / GROUNDEngageDisabled — combat resolution in progress
RESOLUTIONResolving…Disabled — resource collection and turn wrap-up
